#2719. Week 10 Stock Up, Stock Down: Mayeday

Week 10 was one where the lows felt higher than the highs. Drake Maye went down and took the whole Patriots offense with him. Carson Beck started his first game and the impact may have cratered the entire Arizona offense going forward, and Jonathan Taylor just might not escape generic RB1 hell. Let's discuss.

Tyson followed up a 4/30 debut with a triumph of modern target volume, managing 11/80 on 3 targets as no Saints player other than him managed more than five.

The 80 is the key here – I don't think that Tyson needs to go skyrocketing up into the WR2 range based on this. The Saints just aren't playing like that kind of offense right now. But I do think it at least inches into the realm of possibility down the stretch.

We all knew that first-round pick Tyson would get a chance to do this sort of thing, and though the Saints didn't win this game, they did establish that they're willing to use him quite a bit. I'm not quite buying the idea that he is now the offense's No. 1 option and that all Chris Olave shares are headed to the dumpster, but I do think he's going to crowd out some of the other ancillary targets in this offense.

I take no pleasure in noting that RB2 was already down bad enough with four teams on bye to have time-share backs as easy No. 2 runners. The Texans lost Woody Marks to a concussion halfway through Sunday's disastrous loss to the Browns and will now be in line to be Houston's No. 1 back on Thursday night assuming David Montgomery can't get off the mat.

I'm going to level with you here: I don't think Demercado is good. I also don't think the Texans can run the ball well. But this remains to some extent a volume game, and Demercado could be the No. 1 back against a Colts defense that has been dastardly for most of the season. He's not someone to blow the whole FAAB wad on, but Demercado could give you a big game on Thursday before fading back into anonymity.

The Tennessee Titans offense has been … cooking(?) since the bye. They've now scored at least 20 points in each of their last four games, and they're playing the Cowboys next week. I already know that you don't believe me that this is happening, and I understand and accept that. You can skip on to the next capsule to read about someone who matters.

Well, you're still here for some reason. Ayomanor has played at least 50 snaps in each of the last three games, he's found 22 targets over those three games and turned in his first useful box score of the season with 79 scoreless yards against the Jaguars. At the same time, the Titans defense has absolutely collapsed, allowing 40 to the Bengals and Jaguars after the Jeffrey Simmons and Amani Hooker trades.

This team has become a points funnel all of the sudden. And, again, they're playing the Cowboys next week. I'm not telling you Ayomanor is a superstar waiting to be born. But there are six teams on bye next week, and you're going to need to make some weird roster decisions. Ayomanor might just be a good enough WR3 to get you through something next week against Dallas' barely-there defense.

Kansas City's hilarious beatdown of the Falcons culminated in Downs notching 4/53/1, the touchdown being just his second of the season. However, the additional funny context here is that Downs played just 10 offensive snaps in his first game as a Chief.

We've been burned by Downs before, of course, but with Eternal Non-Entity Xavier Worthy in front of him, it's easy to understand that Downs is going to eventually feast on a larger play volume. Is it going to be a Rashee Rice volume? That I'm not yet sure of. But I am pretty sure that Downs is going to do well enough that fantasy managers will be happy.

Going forward, it's going to feel easy to pencil Downs in as a WR3. There's also going to be plenty of runway to grow. The Colts part of his season never happened. Please stop asking about it.

(If you're looking for Emmett Johnson praise, you're late, I did that after Week 8.)

Drake Maye went down with an ankle injury early in the first quarter, effectively sabotaging the offense. A.J. Brown left with his own injury near the end of the game. Neither player returned, and Patriots coach Mike Vrabel deferred to testing. The early news on Maye from PFT was not exactly encouraging.

New England is on bye, of course, which helps the odds that Maye won't miss much time. But if he does miss time – and we've seen enough hints that this might happen – this offense looked dead in the water with Tommy DeVito under center. Unfortunately, when you write this column, you understand that this kind of death comes for a fantasy offense a few times a year.

It would be irresponsible to pretend that we know what kind of absence Maye's looking at, but even if it's not a multi-week one, you can't be starting Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner with DeVito under center. That's just not viable, as we saw today. Tertiary receivers without Brown's health will be tough plays. It's a top-to-bottom tough scene.

Congratulations to Alvin Kamara on his two touchdowns. He saw just 16 snaps in a messy situation and will be hard to trust as a FLEX play going forward. Travis Etienne didn't exactly establish himself as the lead back, but he did muddy up Kamara's receiving situation enough to make Kamara himself only a touchdown-or-bust play.

As for Johnson, in his last four games he has not crossed four targets and has just one pity touchdown to show for a grand total of 69 yards of work over that time frame. This offense is running out of effectiveness and volume to get tertiary targets involved. Perhaps Jordyn Tyson's emergence will cause teams to play them differently, but I don't see how you could pretend to be happy starting Johnson given how his last month of returns have gone. I'd classify Johnson as a TE2 at this point.

Nobody is saying that McBride is unplayable in fantasy football or anything like that, but what we are now dealing with is rookie Carson Beck, and I think there's a reasonable case to make that McBride's overall TE1 ceiling is impacted by this.

To be clear: I wouldn't put an enormous amount of stock in this rogue 5/37 line. The Rams are a great defense, and Myles Garrett is finally healthy. The Cardinals only managed to possess the ball for 17:37 of the 60 minutes of football, which I'm told is very bad.

But given the lack of receiving talent around him and a rookie quarterback who took five sacks and was picked off twice in his first start, I think we at least need to shift the window a bit on what we think will happen going forward. I would expect more 7/85s than 11/135s over the rest of the season with the quarterback and receiver downgrades.

The less I can say about the rest of this receiving corps, the better. Only one other receiver caught more than one ball.

With the Colts really and truly playing out the string here, is there really a reason for them to push Taylor? They seem very content to roll out Seth McGowan for 20 snaps a game and McGowan, to his credit, has taken advantage of the opportunities. He's averaging 4.8 yards per carry on the season and has vultured a score from Taylor in each of the last two weeks. He's not exactly decimating Taylor's workload, but McGowan is doing just enough to make RB1 upside a fading dream for the established vet.

I think Taylor is a great player, but other than the fact that he's going to destroy the Texans on Thursday Night because they have not gotten straight with whatever deity they pray to, why would they push a guy who they might have the next general manager move next offseason? To what end? If they weren't going to pedal Taylor to the floor against the Dolphins to get a win, there's no reason to believe that'll happen the rest of the season.

Will he be a reasonable RB1? Of course he will. But the guy who might threaten the overall RB1 ranks? He might have had his last hurrah against the Falcons in Europe roughly a year ago. This is just a steady contributor profile, no more, no less.

#2715. Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid

Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Jaylen Brown-Tyrese Maxey duo starred, LeBron James reached another milestone, and the Sixers earned a win without Joel Embiid on Sunday afternoon.

They improved to 11-3 on the season with a 131-124 victory over the Pacers at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

Brown scored 31 points and Maxey posted 27.

LeBron James had 15 points and 11 assists. He passed Jason Kidd on Sunday for third in NBA history with 12,092 assists.

Pascal Siakam scored 31 points for the 5-9 Pacers.

On the first day of a back-to-back, the Sixers were down Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pacers' injured players included Tyrese Haliburton and Andrew Nembhard.

The Sixers will face the Nets on Monday night in Brooklyn. Here are observations on their win over the Pacers:

Jabari Walker started for the first time this season, opening the game at center. He's been in the Sixers' rotation the past five games since Bona's injury.

Walker set up the Sixers' first basket, swiping a steal and then tossing the ball ahead to Maxey for a fast-break dunk. Maxey and Brown both began well and combined to score all of the Sixers' first 15 points.

Though he conceded five inches to 7-foot Pacers center Ivica Zubac, Walker was solid in his first stint. He got an early post stop on Zubac and then snatched a strong defensive rebound.

Dean Wade was next up for the Sixers at the five. He sunk a three-pointer on his first shot to give the team a 20-16 lead.

Walker ended up playing 25 minutes and posting 11 points and seven rebounds. Going back to the preseason, his stock has steadily risen.

"Here we are again after another game saying Jabari played very well," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "He plays hard, he rebounds, he's got another level of confidence with his shooting this year.

"It's kind of wash, rinse and repeat again with him (today). He was great. … Jabari went in there and battled (Zubac). I thought he certainly matched him, if not outplayed him, which is a heck of a job."

Wade had 12 points and seven boards in 35 minutes. Overall, the Sixers' lack of healthy conventional centers is still a clear deficiency. Of course, everything should be simpler once Embiid is back in action.

The Sixers' defense did not have a sparkling start. The Pacers tallied 35 points in the first quarter and shot 62.5 percent from the field.

Brown helped the Sixers avoid a substantial deficit by draining all sorts of jumpers. He rarely appears bothered by close contests. Brown moved to 7 for 9 from the floor when he knocked down a three early in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope's triple knotted the contest up at 37-all.

Nurse needed to stray from his Plan A rotation when VJ Edgecombe picked up his third foul with 9:56 left in the second quarter. Labaron Philon Jr., who got a game with the G League's Delaware Blue Coats on Friday night, subbed in.

For a rookie guard, Philon has looked comfortable and confident on offense in most of his NBA appearances. He swished a long-range jumper in the second quarter and saw a floater rim out.

Brown reached the 20-point mark and put the Sixers up one with a slam assisted by James late in the second quarter.

He ran into serious foul trouble in the third quarter. Brown was whistled for his fourth foul with 9:53 left in the period for an off-arm shove on Aaron Nesmith. Wade entered and Brown exited.

The Sixers' slim lead didn't slip away. Walker nailed threes on consecutive possessions and Maxey jammed in a dunk.

Soon after, Tacko Fall came in for his first meaningful minutes as a Sixer. The 7-foot-6 two-way contract player grabbed an offensive board off a missed Edgecombe free throw, which drew one of the day's loudest cheers. With Fall on the floor, Maxey and James connected on an alley-oop that extended the Sixers' lead to 82-73.

When the Sixers tried to sit in a zone, Fall was called for a defensive three-second violation. Whatever the scheme, most of Fall's defensive work will come around the paint. He certainly has exceptional physical traits as a rim protector and is not nimble on the perimeter.

Fall logged five scoreless third-quarter minutes and recorded three rebounds. The Sixers outscored Indiana by a point with Fall on the court. Given Fall is occupying a (two-way) roster slot and the Sixers are so depleted at center, it made sense to see a bit of what he can do outside of garbage time. While five minutes isn't enough for any grand conclusions, it's very safe to say Fall is a unique player.

"I'm 7-6, so I can change the game in so many ways," Fall said. "Offensively, setting screens, making sure guys get open, being an easy target for lobs. Defensively, I feel like I've always been an elite rim protector and I've worked on my body a lot to be able to move a lot better."

Nurse praised Fall's outing, saying he "gave us some great minutes and a nice lift."

Fall is appreciative of his first NBA opportunity since the 2021-22 season.

"I've worked very hard," he said. "God has brought me back here and I'm thankful. And I'm ready. Whenever my name is called, I'm going to go out there and do my job."

The Sixers built their advantage to 102-87 with a Brown three early in the fourth quarter. They couldn't cruise to a blowout, though.

Siakam kept hurting the Sixers as a driver and had a highly efficient fourth quarter, scoring 19 points on 7-for-9 shooting. Quenton Jackson's layup trimmed Indiana's deficit to 119-115.

The Sixers ultimately held off the Pacers' push.

Caldwell-Pope canned a three, Wade threw down an and-one dunk, and James checked off his milestone assist with a late dish to Edgecombe for a layup.

With another late, fourth-quarter comeback, Cleveland defeated Houston 27-24 for the club’s sixth win of the season.

The Browns got down 17-0 early, but scored 20 straight points to take a 20-17 lead late in the third quarter.

Then on the next play, Quinshon Judkins punched it in for a 5-yard, go-ahead score to put the Browns up by three.

The Texans had a chance to tie it up with a field goal, getting the ball back with 47 seconds on the clock. But after getting a first down, Houston couldn’t move the ball any further and C.J. Stroud’s final fourth-down pass fell incomplete for a turnover on downs.

Houston scored just once after putting up 17 points on its first three drives. Stroud finished the game 20-of-38 for 211 yards with three touchdowns and one interception. Nico Collins had nine catches for 94 yards with a TD.

On the other side, Watson completed 25-of-40 passes for 312 yards with a touchdown. He was the team’s leading rusher with 49 yards on eight carries with a TD. Fannin led with 91 yards on seven catches.

With the win, the Browns head into their Week 11 bye at 6-4. As noted on the Fox broadcast, Cleveland is now 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963. They will next host the Raiders in Week 12.

The 3-6 Texans have a short week upcoming, as they’ll play the Colts on Thursday night.

#2710. 5 Blockbuster Reasons To Watch ONE SAMURAI 5 On November 18

Gold on the line, a home crowd on its feet, and a card full of fighters with something to prove. ONE SAMURAI 5 is ready to take over Tokyo.

The action goes down at EBARA WAVE Arena Ota on Wednesday, November 18, and it is built to leave fans breathless from the opening bell. The all-explosive card will be headlined by an epic ONE World Title fight alongside nine additional MMA, Muay Thai, and kickboxing barnburners.

Japan's brightest names share the global stage with challengers from abroad, and nearly every matchup carries a score to settle or a reputation to build.

Here are five electrifying reasons to circle the date.

Joshua "The Passion" Pacio has been a fixture at the top of the strawweight division for years. The Filipino star first won ONE gold at 22 and has since become a three-time ONE Strawweight MMA World Champion.

The belt has changed hands along the way, but he has always found a path back to it. The Lions Nation MMA co-founder's fights on the global stage last just over six minutes on average – a testament to the 19 finishes he has racked up throughout his career, with more than half of them coming under the promotional banner.

In his last outing, the 30-year-old defended his gold with a rear-naked choke win against Mansur Malachiev in their rematch. Now, he takes on a challenger with real momentum. Keito "Pocket Monk" Yamakita has won five in succession leading up to this epic ONE Strawweight MMA World Title clash.

The Reversal Gym Shinjuku Me star won his first seven fights without a loss, and he carried that unbeaten run into ONE in 2023. Since then, he has built his name on dragging opponents to the mat and making them pay once they are there, with submissions as the preferred finish. His five-fight winning streak includes a victory over former divisional king Yosuke "The Ninja" Saruta.

Pacio's explosive wushu-rooted striking meets Yamakita's relentless takedown pressure, and the home crowd will be roaring for every scramble. One man defends a legacy, the other chases a dream, and the gold hangs in the balance.

Being the younger brother of Japanese kickboxing star Tenshin Nasukawa comes with expectations, but Ryujin "SHINDO" Nasukawa has spent his young career meeting them on his own terms.

The 20-year-old has collected the ISKA K-1 Strawweight Championship, along with RISE titles at flyweight and super flyweight. The TEPPEN GYM talent pairs a stiff jab and punishing body shots with the patience to wait for his openings, and he showed all of it in his ONE debut at The Inner Circle 23.

He promised a finish, then delivered it in round two, when a right hook and a knee to the body sent Thongpoon PK Saenchai to the ropes and a flurry forced the stoppage. Now he returns to Japan in a strawweight kickboxing co-main event, and the 18-year-old promotional newcomer waiting across from him is no easy welcome.

Raichi Nagai arrives on a tear, with a knockout win in his most recent outing against the reigning champion to claim the NJKF title. The young gun now takes that confidence into the biggest opportunity of his career.

Fans can expect a blistering pace when this clash gets underway at ONE SAMURAI 5. Ryujin brings explosive speed and heavy pressure, and Raichi is cut from much the same cloth, with six of his nine wins coming by knockout. Neither man is likely to let the other settle into a rhythm, and both are happy to trade in the pocket. With two quick, hard-hitting strikers meeting in the middle, the finish could arrive at any moment.

Greatness does not disappear overnight, and Jarred "The Monkey God" Brooks is determined to prove it at EBARA WAVE Arena Ota this week.

The 33-year-old burst into ONE in 2021 and left a trail of victories in his wake. He then outworked Pacio across five rounds at ONE 164 to become the ONE Strawweight MMA World Champion, and his larger-than-life personality made him one of the most recognizable names on the roster. The years that followed tested him, though. He lost his gold, then captured the interim crown, but he has since suffered the toughest stretch of his career with three successive defeats.

For a man who built his identity on winning, the road back has demanded more than skill, and it has all been leading to this comeback. Waiting to spoil it is Tatsumitsu "The Sweeper" Wada, a 38-year-old who has been a ONE mainstay since 2019.

The former DEEP champion has tested himself against some of the best in the division. He reached the semifinals of the 2019 ONE Flyweight MMA World Grand Prix, and he took one of the sport's all-time greats, Demetrious "Mighty Mouse" Johnson, the full three rounds. That kind of experience does not fade, and it makes him a difficult puzzle for anyone.

"The Monkey God" is chasing a revival and Wada is chasing momentum, but only one of them will get what they came for in Tokyo.

Former ONE Bantamweight Kickboxing World Champion Petchtanong Petchfergus has long been one of the most polished strikers. The Thai veteran has built his reputation on razor-sharp timing, technical precision, and the kind of fight IQ that cannot be taught.

Those tools have kept him in the title conversation ever since, including a second-round stoppage of former champion Alaverdi Ramazanov in 2024 that proved the sharpness had not faded. A setback against Yuki Yoza slowed that push, but it did not dent his resolve. In May, he bounced back with a composed three-round performance against Ben "The Problem" Woolliss.

Waiting for him in his switch to featherweight kickboxing is a rising Japanese star who has already proven he can take down a legend. Yutaro Asahi opened his promotional account by becoming the first fighter to beat Seksan "The Man Who Yields To No One" Or Kwanmuang in ONE.

Over three hard-fought rounds of Muay Thai, he dropped the Thai icon with a lead uppercut and a left hand, and his footwork and angles kept him a step ahead through the final bell.

The stylistic clash is a fascinating one. Petchtanong brings veteran fight IQ, power, and explosiveness, while Asahi counters with movement, creativity, and clever angles. Another legendary scalp would make it impossible to call his first one a fluke.

Besides Yamakita, Ryujin, Raichi, Wada, and Asahi, ONE SAMURAI 5 boasts a deep roster of Japanese talent looking to deliver another night to remember for their compatriots.

Knockout artist Yugo Kato is chasing a third highlight-reel win on the global stage when he meets Jurai Ishii in strawweight Muay Thai. The 27-year-old can expect a stern challenge, though, against the 21-year-old Ishii, who has shown his finishing power across three outings in the organization.

In bantamweight kickboxing, Gump "Mr. No Damage" looks to push his unbeaten record in ONE to 3-0 against debutant Shuto Inui. Elsewhere, 19-year-old Reiji, flawless through two appearances, faces his sternest test yet in Portuguese bruiser Rui Botelho.

The featherweight MMA bout pairs two hungry fresh faces as Shosuke Kinoshita meets Takuya Shibamura. Then comes a heavyweight MMA showdown between two menacing finishers. Ryugo "Rising Rock Star" Takeuchi owns five finishes, while fellow Japanese star Brandon Hashimoto, making his ONE debut, has six.

Whatever style fans prefer, the spectacle has something for everyone, from world-class kickboxing exchanges and Muay Thai wars to intriguing MMA fights. With a World Title on top and a deep slate of Japanese talent beneath it, Wednesday in Tokyo is shaping up to be an unforgettable evening.

#2706. Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics

Sixers, Brown have a 'humbling' night in loss to Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Whatever Jaylen Brown and the Sixers dreamed up for their first matchup against the Celtics soon flew out the window on Tuesday night.

Brown was whistled for two early fouls, the Sixers fell behind and their early-season flaws were on full display in a 123-101 loss at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

"We've just got to get better," Brown said. "Tonight was humbling. We got outplayed, out-executed. So we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the next one."

Over 26 minutes, Brown had 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting and five rebounds against the team that traded him away this summer.

As for the endless dissection of his relationship with former co-star Jayson Tatum, Brown didn't have much to add Tuesday. There was no public reconciliation, no obvious on-court animosity and generally nothing to satisfy fans hoping for some kind of fireworks on that front.

"I'm just focused on doing what's best for my team," Brown said. "Everything else … to be honest, I wasn't paying attention. But credit to Jayson; he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics. They executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and they were the better team tonight."

Tatum scored 21 points, two of which came on a third-quarter slam over LeBron James. Paul George continued his fantastic start as a Celtic by dropping 36 points and draining six three-pointers.

The Celtics dominated from beyond the arc, shooting 22 for 49 (44.9 percent). The Sixers went just 11 for 37 (29.7 percent) on another night of underwhelming offense. The team sits 22nd in the NBA in offensive rating, 24th in three-point makes per game and 21st in three-point percentage.

"I think that we've got some guys that are obviously shooting much lower percentages than their last season or their career average — almost a handful of guys," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "And I don't think it's because they're shooting fallaway, totally contested ones. I think they're shots we want them to take. So I think they'll continue to take 'em and I'm pretty sure those will even out into their career averages."

Joel Embiid is at 37 percent from the floor and 4 for 33 from three-point range (12.1 percent).

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center got through an injury scare when he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter and hit a three early in the third. It was his first long-range make since the Sixers' home opener back on Oct. 22.

"It's a work in progress," Embiid said. "I think the biggest thing is just not thinking. I'm probably overthinking it. The rhythm of the game is different. I'm so used to having to create for myself, so it's a little bit different.

"But I think I'm slowly getting better. You could see as soon as I made a three, the next shot in the short corner … I didn't even think about it. I just shot it and let it fly, and I made it. … I think it's just about taking what's in front of you. Make or miss, keep working on your game. It's going to get there at some point."

Even with the Sixers second in the Eastern Conference standings at 9-3, Embiid believes the team's defense has "slacked off a little bit" in recent games.

"I don't really look at the record," he said. "I just look at the process of, 'Are we getting better every day?' We can always do a better job at all phases of the game."

"They're one of the top teams in the league and they've been together for a while," Brown said. "We've got a lot to work on over here, so we've got to get to work."

The Sixers will face the Raptors on Thursday night in Philadelphia.

They'll have to wait until Jan. 21 in Boston to see the Celtics again.

"I was looking forward to this," Brown said. "I was looking forward to playing well, but s— happens. Just get ready for the next one."

#2703. Mike Macdonald Has Candid Message for Raiders After Seahawks Win

The Seattle Seahawks were in a challenging game against the Las Vegas Raiders. In the first half, the Seahawks only recorded seven points, but despite the underwhelming performance, it was in the third quarter that Seattle established their dominance, which led to their 21-13 win in Week 10.

Seattle recorded 14 points in their third quarter, and in the second half, the Seahawks defense limited the Raiders offense to three points. This mix was enough for the Seahawks to get the win and move to 6-4.

Nonetheless, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald spoke after the win and had a candid message for the Raiders and their head coach, Klint Kubiak, who was on his coaching staff last season as the offensive coordinator.

"I love Klint," Macdonald said postgame on Nov. 15. "All those guys we weren't able to retain who went with them, we love those guys. They're doing a great job. This is a good football team. They're well coached and tough. It's tough for a rookie quarterback in our league to come in and play after not playing for nine weeks. But I thought he played well. He's got a great future."

Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first regular-season start, went 17-for-29 on his pass attempts, leading to 143 passing yards, one rushing touchdown, and a passer rating of 71.5. Moreover, the Seahawks were able to sack him six times.

Macdonald shared more kind words about the Raiders coaching staff that he has a previous relationship with, as it was a competitive contest between him and those on his staff from last season.

"We're getting after it when we tee it up and get between the white lines," Macdonald added. "But one of the reasons we do this goes beyond football. These are relationships that we'll have forever. Those are guys who are really good people, and they have the right stuff. I'm proud of how they do business, and I'm proud to be associated with them, as well as our coaches."

Meanwhile, Seahawks backup QB Drew Lock was effective on the times he needed to throw the ball, going 14-for-17 on his pass attempts for 240 yards, two touchdowns, and posting a passer rating of 158.0.

After the win, Lock spoke about the team's performance as they were able to weather the storm in the first half.

"I think it just goes back to the style of football that we play," Lock told CBS Sports postgame. "If we jump out on you early, we're going to believe it's going to be a long day. But if we don't, our mentality coming out of halftime is that this is going to be our half. Whatever we want to do when we get out there, we can go do it. We just have to execute.

"We're shooting ourselves in the foot, and I think we did that a little bit. Enough to win, but not enough to put the game away, which made it a little nerve-wracking at the end. But it was a good second half. We have to find ways to keep getting better."

#2691. JJ Redick not pleased after Lakers nearly blow 31-point lead to Suns

It was a "disservice" for the Lakers to nearly blow what appeared to be an insurmountable 31-point lead. He said that playing "to our standards" is what's expected from the Lakers — and seeing a huge lead sliced to five points didn't reflect that.

Yes, the Lakers are tied for the best record in the NBA at 12-2. Yes, they have won eight straight games. And yes, his team has one of the best offensive engines in the league in Luka Doncic.

Even with all that and a 131-123 win over the Phoenix Suns, Lakers coach JJ Redick wasn't pleased with what he saw in the fourth quarter Sunday.

Read more: While tied for NBA's best record, Lakers believe they can be better

"We're working too hard and we're playing too hard to build these leads," Redick said. "It's a disservice to each other to take your foot off the gas. You have to play for 48 minutes and we're going to need our defense to win us games. ... Gotta be better in the fourth quarter."

Behind Doncic's sizzling first quarter that led to 43 points, the Lakers opened a 101-70 lead with 1:47 left in the third quarter.

Then came a letdown by the Lakers amid an onslaught from the Suns.

The Suns scored 43 points in the fourth, shot 50% from the field and pulled to within 126-121 with 1:05 left on a layup by Collin Gillespie, who had 13 of his 26 points in the final frame.

Matisse Thybulle of the Lakers blocks the shot of Devin Booker in the first half Sunday. (Kelsey Grant / Getty Images)

The Lakers have been down this road before, losing to Golden State after blowing a 25-point lead.

"You go up 30, it's easy to be like, 'You know, the game is over. They're not going to come back.' But it's very easy in the NBA for teams to come back and make runs because this is the game of runs," Jake LaRavia said. "So again, we just have to do a better job at staying in it for the full 48 minutes and being able to complete a full game."

It took two big plays from Quentin Grimes for the Lakers to not blow the game.

Grimes collected an offensive rebound after LaRavia missed a three-pointer and then pulled up and banked in a three-pointer for a 129-121 Lakers lead with 33.7 seconds left.

Grimes had 22 points on seven-for-10 shooting, going five for six on three-pointers. After missing the previous two games with a right finger injury, he saved the Lakers.

Read more: Lakers' Austin Reaves considered day-to-day with heel injury

He was asked if he called "bank" on his final three.

"I called game. I called game. I called game," said Grimes, smiling. "No, I mean, the bank ain't open on Sunday. I called game. Trying to get out of here and get back to L.A."

Doncic had 20 points in the first quarter, going five for 10 from the field. He leads the NBA in first-quarter scoring (13.6) and in scoring per game (38.6). It was just another masterpiece for Doncic, who was serenaded with "MVP, MVP" chants twice from some fans.

"It was very nice," Doncic said. "I think everybody can see my smile at the free-throw line. And so, that made me happy, honestly."

The Lakers entered the game with three days off after road wins over Detroit, Atlanta and Milwaukee.

"I don't think we should put a ceiling on this group," Redick said. "This group is committed to getting better every single day, recognizing that this is a process to become a high-level team, and that's what I want from this group ... hold each other to that standard every single time.

"And, honestly, that's the frustrating part at times because you see how good we can be. There's no reason to ever play less than that standard."

Lakers guard Austin Reaves missed the game with a left heel contusion/bone bruise.

#2687. Jaxon Smith-Njigba should be taken seriously as an MVP candidate

As trophy typos go, it’s one thing to have a mistake on “offensive player of the year.” A three-letter award is harder to screw up.

And, frankly, Seahawks receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba should be taken very seriously as an MVP candidate.

Sure, no receiver has ever won the NFL MVP award. No receiver has ever done what he’s doing, either.

With 171 yards and a touchdown on Sunday against the Raiders, Smith-Njigba has 1,206 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns through 10 games. No one has done that since 1960.

Think about that. Think of all the great receivers who have played since the NFL relaxed the rules to promote more passing. Even then, only three players had ever gotten to 1,200 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns in 10 games before today: Don Hutson in 1942, Elroy “Crazy Legs” Hirsch in 1951, and Raymond Berry in 1960.

Smith-Njigba remains on pace to set the new single-season receiving yardage record. And to become the first player in league history with 2,000 or more receiving yards in a season.

Often, a receiver who has a special season loses MVP votes to the quarterback who fed him the passes. With the Seahawks using both Sam Darnold and Drew Lock, neither will be taking MVP votes away from anyone.

Then there’s the official definition of MVP: “The player who was most valuable to their team over the course of the season.” Smith-Njigba accounts for more than half of the Seattle passing offense. Even when everyone knows the ball is coming to him, he still makes plays.

For now, those inclined to wager on the MVP winner haven’t taken JSN seriously. His odds to win the award are 80-1.

That should change. Because JSN should be regarded as a very real threat to win the MVP award.

#2685. Seahawks shut down Raiders in second half of 21-13 win

Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start started with a bang, but the Seahawks slammed the door on him in the second half on Sunday.

Mendoza ran for a touchdown to open the game helped the Raiders to a 10-7 lead over the defending champions through 30 minutes of play in Las Vegas. The second half was a very different story, however.

The Raiders were shut out until a Matt Gay field goal with 2:04 left to play in the game and the Seahawks scored a pair of touchdowns to pick up a 21-13 win. The victory pushes their record to 6-4 as they head into their bye week and it came after one of the smartest special teams plays we’re likely to see this season.

After Gay’s field goal, Seahawks returner Tory Horton jumped to bat the ensuing kickoff back in bounds rather than let it sail out for a touchback. He also had the presence of mind to tell Rashid Shaheed to return the ball since he stepped out of bounds and couldn’t do it himself. The play wound up taking the clock through the two-minute warning, which meant the Raiders could only stop the clock twice rather than three times.

The Seahawks only ran 17 offensive plays in the first half of the game, but they found their footing behind Zach Charbonnet and Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the second half. Charbonnet ran 12 times for 55 yards and Smith-Njigba continued his remarkable season with seven catches for 160 yards after the break. One of those was a 71-yard touchdown from Drew Lock.

All in all, Seattle picked up 274 yards in the final two quarters while holding the Raiders to 27 yards on their final six possessions. They sacked Mendoza four times in the second half and the loss of tight end Brock Bowers to an ankle injury left the rookie without real options in the passing game.

Mendoza, who finished 17-of-29 for 143 yards, will now try for his first win in Denver next weekend.

#2683. Lakers survive Suns’ furious rally behind Luka Doncic’s 43-point night

PHOENIX — The 21-page presentation toward the beginning of their three-day break from games came with a simple message: Even though the Lakers were tied for the best record and had the league's best offense, they could be even better.

Despite being without Austin Reaves as he allows the bruise in his left heel to recover, the Lakers showed for most of their 131-123 victory over the Suns Sunday afternoon what their better could look like.

Luka Dončić #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts during an NBA game against the Phoenix Suns in Phoenix, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images

They also showed more progress needs to be made after they nearly blew a 31-point second-half lead.

The Lakers rode the momentum of another hot start from Luka Dončić (43 points, nine assists) and precise execution to their eighth straight victory to put them at a league-best 12-2 on the season.

Luka Dončić (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts during an NBA game against the Phoenix Suns on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in Phoenix. Getty Images

Dončić had 20 points of his scoring total in the first quarter, which was not only his second 20-point opening quarter of the season but also made him the only player in the league with multiple 20-point first quarters.

And after the non-Dončić minutes had been a sore spot for the Lakers for most of the season, they flipped the script on Sunday.

They won the minutes Dončić was on the bench in the second quarter, helping them take a 64-54 lead going into halftime, 101-70 lead late in the third and 104-80 lead going into the fourth.

But the Lakers didn't find the same success when Dončić wasn't in the game to start the fourth.

By the time the Slovenian star subbed back in with 6:48 remaining, the Suns had the momentum after trimming their deficit to 14 points, and eventually six points multiple times late in the fourth.

Luka Dončić #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers controls the ball against Jordan Goodwin #23 of the Phoenix Suns in Phoenix on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images

Dončić's late-game offensive heroics, in addition to the Suns missing three free throws in the final two minutes, ensured the Lakers didn't relinquish the lead and held on for the wire-to-wire victory.

Quentin Grimes (22 points) came up with an offensive rebound and banked in a 3-pointer with 34 seconds left to ice the game for the Lakers.

Walker Kessler (14 points, 12 rebounds), Matisse Thybulle (12 points) and Jake LaRavia (12 points) all scored at least 12 points, putting all of the Lakers' starters in double figures in scoring.

Collin Sexton added 16 points and three assists off the bench.

#2676. NBA News: Jaylen Clark out 2 weeks

After an abysmal performance against a basement-dwelling Chicago Bulls team on Saturday night, things got worse the next day. The Minnesota Timberwolves officially announced that Jaylen Clark, our favorite try-hard defensive stopper, would miss the next two weeks at minimum with a right hamstring strain.

Here's the play where Clark got injured early in the second quarter, making a hustle play and diving into the Minnesota bench.

This is certainly something that will be a significant blow to the Wolves. Though Clark averages just over 13 minutes per game, he is fourth on the team in defensive rating (100.3). He's been one of, if not the best, on-ball defender for Minnesota. He constantly injects energy into his team when they need it most. Jaylen has also been a 36% three-point shooter so far this season, acting as a valuable release valve on the perimeter.

"Clark County" will miss at least the next eight games in the next 14 days before he's reevaluated. Soft tissue injuries are notoriously easy to reaggravate, thus it's safe to expect he will miss well over double-digit games. When you consider Jaylen's style of play – lots of quick burst lateral movement – he could be on the shelf for at least a month next to Anthony Edwards and Donte DiVincenzo.

So who will step up in the rotation from the depth chart?

I have long since been a fan of two-way guard Zyon Pullin, but he is certainly an offense-oriented player who doesn't really provide what Clark does. Rookie Isaiah Evans is earning his stripes in the G League and likely one of the less effective defensive players on the roster. I could easily see Finch divvying Jaylen's minutes over to currently involved players like Bones Hyland and Terrence Shannon Jr.

But can I make a quick case for "no longer the worst player in the NBA," Cody Williams?

The younger Williams brother has appeared in just seven of 13 games for the Wolves this season, all in "development time." However, he did show multiple flashes of his potential during the preseason. Cody impressed in a spot preseason start against the reigning champion New York Knicks, locking up 2026 Finals MVP Jalen Brunson.

Zach Lowe had a lot of positive things to say about Williams, including his defensive improvement, at the end of last season. I'm not calling for Williams to soak up Clark's entire 13 minute role, but he fits what Minnesota is losing in Clark the most. Here's a list of guards the Wolves will face in the next two to three weeks:

There will certainly be times where LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels, Ayo Dosunmu, or Bones Hyland either falls into foul trouble or just need relief guarding those difficult assignments. When that happens, the need to get an active body who is athletic and long will be especially important.

This is the opportunity that many players in Cody's shoes hope for. He's still just 20 years old (soon to be 21 this week), but has years of experience under his belt for a tanking team. Minnesota will need his services out of desperation and he can shed that early career label as a draft bust. It's the perfect storm of supply meeting demand.

Williams also wears jersey number 9 which, as we all know, is a magical number.

If it were up to you, who would you most like to see replace Clark's minutes? Are you on the Cody Caboose like me? Or do you prefer another option? What is Ricky Rubio up to these days?

#2671. San Antonio vs. Utah, Final Score: Harper leads Spurs’ final push past Jazz, 110-102

Ascending star Dylan Harper scored 16 of his team's last 24 points to help San Antonio (12-2) claim its 12th straight victory and third straight this season over the Jazz. With the game still very much in doubt, Victor Wembanyama hit a fadeaway jumper and blocked a Keyonte George floater, and Keldon Johnson saved the ensuing carom from falling out of bounds and chased down an offensive rebound at the other end and scored a putback to put the Spurs up four in the penultimate seconds.

In a game with an exasperating amount of runs that were often one after another, Utah staged a 19-7 run spanning hte third and fourth quarters to erase the Spurs' biggest lead of the night (9) and get into the driver's seat until the visitors made that final 24-13 push.

Harper (31 points, 9 assists, and 4 assists) single-handedly willed San Antonio to victory with audacious and self-assured shotmaking throughout those critical fourth quarter minutes. Wembanyama (23 points, 9 rebounds, 5 assists, and 4 blocks) carried the offenisve production throughout the first three quarters. Stephon Castle (20 points, 9 assists, and 4 steals) and reserve Jordan McLaughlin (10 points) assured Fox wouldn't be missed TOO much. Johnson (11 points and 10 rebounds) was a menacing presence for the Spurs in the second half and especially in the waning moments.

Mo Bamba (26 points [6-for-6 from three], 5 rebounds, and 4 assists) performed admirably again in the absence of the star-studded Jazz starting bigs. Backup Brice Sensabaugh (14 points and 7 rebounds) and rookie Darryn Peterson (17 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists) led a group of contributors that supplied plentiful support for Bamba and made up for an off-night for Keyonte George (13 points, 8 assists, and 4 rebounds).

The teams mirrored each other over the opening minutes – with Wembanyama and Bamba taking center stage before Rutgers' Harper and Bailey exchanged buckets. While the bigs' turned away several shots at or near the rim, the Jazz swingmen made a flurry of threes to get themselves out front. Despite those outside bursts, the Spurs stayed neck-and-neck with their counterparts. While the hosts shot an astounding 7-for-10 fron behind the line, they still only went to the second up two, after McLaughlin kickstarted a closing 8-0 run to end the first quarter.

Bamba's third and fourth threes (without a miss) created some space between his team and San Antonio. While the teams continued to shoot well from the field, Utah's proficiency from distance made up the bulk of their advantage. After opposing 9-0 runs, the Jazz took advantage of San Antonio's errant shooting to leap back into the lead. Utah's perimeter men seemed to make quite a few shots late in the clock. Wembanyama rescued a handful of possessions with his shooting and playmaking and the Spurs went to halftime slightly up 58-55.

Coming out of the break, Castle figured in one each of the Spurs' first four scores – two field goals, two freebies, and one assist. Rookie Peterson dazzled with his ability to score from different spots on the floor. Bamba and Bradley resembled Utah legend Thurl Bailey by knocking down shot after shot. A 10-0 run by San Antonio got them to 79-70. Bamba's fifth straight three without a miss tied things right back at 79. San Antonio nearly went the rest of the quarter without scoring again and the teams were deadlocked at 81 going to the final 12 minutes.

Game Clinching Play #1: Everything Harper died from the 8:07 mark of the fourth quarter to the final buzzer.

Game Clinching Play #2: With a four-point lead, Castle received a 'thank you very much' steal and threw down an uncontested windmill jam

I might be repeating myself, but Bamba continues to look like a very competent veteran out there filling in for Markkanen and Jackson, Jr.

The mountain outline on the court is immaculate despite all of the trauma those 90s Jazz teams caused us Spurs fans.

Small sample size of Fox's steady consistency… six first half turnovers in his absence.

The in-arena cams during the first timeout showcased a dance contest, and well, I won't get back those two minutes ever again.

On the Jazz broadcast, they brought in former slam dunk champion Jeremy Evans for a lengthy first half interview. #obscure2010splayers

Area 51 Sequence of the Game: Though the two hadn't found each other over many of the first 23 minutes, Castle fed Wembanyama in transition in the final minute of the half to close out the scoring.

Sequence of the Game #1: At the end of a 10-0 run late in the third quarter, Keldon Johnson – after scoring two straight lay-ups at the rim – lofted a high lob to Luke Kornet and the big man gently lowered the ball into the rim to make it 79-70.

Sequence of the Game #2: After a Castle steal early in the fourth quarter, the guard had a 3-on-1 fast break with Wembanyama and Harper on opposing wings and chose the Rutgers second-year man for a lay-up.

Bamba and Wembanyama (say their names ten times in a row) matched opening pairs of buckets from the tip. The former Rutgers players – Bailey and Harper – traded field goals after that. However, a trio of Jazz triples put them up six. Over several possessions, Wembanyama had some nice two-man action with Vassell and Jordan McLaughlin to mixed results. After dribbling the ball for nearly 20 seconds, Castle willed home a floater. Sensabaugh, like he seems to always do against San Antonio, knocked down a pair of jumpers in the paint to keep the Jazz ahead. Tony Bradley joined a sextet of Jazz players to knock down threes. McLaughlin sandwiched field goals around a Wembanyama three, and despite the Jazz shooting 57% from the field (64% from three), the Spurs ended the quarter down just 31-33.

Bamba's third straight triple put Utah back up five to start the second. Wembanyana's catch-and-shoot three knotted things briefly at 38. After weathering nine straight from the Jazz, San Antonio answered right back with nine of their own. The Spurs failed to convert several chances to tie the game or re-take the lead. Wembanyama took his time on the right block and tossed up a bankshot-and-1 over Bamba that would have made Tim Duncan proud. Johnson's transition three put San Antonio up one. While the Jazz executed well over the bulk of the first half minutes, an Area 51 transition lob slam made it 58-55 Spurs at the break.

At the start of the third, Castle followed two quick baskets with a couple of free throws and assisted Harper's and-1 to briefly get the San Antonio lead to ten. Undeterred, Peterson capped a 10-0 Utah avalanche with a corner three and a floater to tie things at 67. The Spurs, with Johnson's prominent contributions, generated their own 10-0 run while Wembanyama sat to go up 79-70. San Antonio stayed stuck at 79 and was nearly shut out the rest of the quarter aside from some Castle free throws, and the Jazz pulled even at 81 heading to the fourth.

#2662. Game Recap: Furious comeback by Suns bench falls short in 131-123 loss

The Lakers came out of the gates hot, and the Suns did not. From there, every time the Suns started to put together a run, the Lakers answered with a bigger run. And while the bench gave the Suns some hope with a furious comeback attempt in the fourth quarter, the Suns dug themselves far too big a hole to climb out of, ultimately falling to the Lakers at home, 131-123.

If the Suns had any hope of an upset, they needed to slow down the Lakers' potent offense, and they failed to do that for much of the afternoon. The Lakers came out of the gates hot and did not really slow down. Luka scored 20 in the first quarter on the way to a 43-point afternoon (together with nine assists), but the Suns' inability to stop Lakers not named Luka, inability to keep the Lakers off the offensive boards, and inability to stop the three is what ultimately did the team in.

Quentin Grimes scored 22 points for the Lakers, including 11 in the third quarter, while shooting 5-of-6 from three. The Lakers grabbed 12 offensive rebounds – with Walker Kessler having six of them – which led to 21 second-chance points. And the Lakers shot 16-of-41 (39%) from three, with Luka and Grimes combining to hit 10 of them.

For the Suns, the story was the fact that the starters dug such a deep hole that the bench could not get them out. Devin Booker was 4-14, Jalen Green was 4-11, and Dillon Brooks was 0-of-2 (what?!). The Suns actually out-rebounded the Lakers (42 to 40) and grabbed more offensive rebounds than the Lakers (14 to 12), but not thanks to the starters. The bench grabbed 29 of the Suns' 42 rebounds and 12 of their 14 offensive rebounds. But the Suns' bench not only outperformed the starters on the boards, but they also outperformed them overall.

Collin Gillespie led the Suns in scoring with 26 points (including 5-of-10 from three). Jordan Goodwin led the team in rebounds, with seven. Ryan Dunn grabbed four offensive rebounds, and Luke Kennard chipped in another three.

And let's not forget Koa Peat. Mr. Arizona sparked a furious fourth-quarter rally that saw the Suns' bench cut a 24-point Lakers lead to just five, before running out of steam down the stretch.

Overall, this game ended up being much closer than it felt throughout the afternoon. The Suns started the fourth quarter down by 24, and the bench was entirely responsible for the team nearly pulling this one out. Notably, Jordan Ott stuck with the bench throughout that quarter. He did not go back to the starters. It felt like the right move, but also truly confirms the lack of cohesiveness with the starting five.

At the end of the day, the Suns miss out on a chance to get to .500, falling to 5-7, as the Lakers win their eighth in a row to move to 12-2.

The Suns got off to the slowest start we've seen since opening night, letting the Lakers score the first 10 points of the game — eight of them by Luka — before Miles Bridges scored the team's first points with 9:24 left in the first quarter. The Lakers followed that 10-2 start by going on a 13-3 run, which left the Suns trailing by 18 after just over 5 minutes of playing time.

Jordan Ott went to the bench, and the bench and Devin Booker managed to trim that lead to 9 by the end of the quarter. A Booker jumper, a Collin Gillespie three, then a Kahman Maluach layup on a nice feed from Book sparked a 7-0 run, to make it a 23-12 game. From there, Book and Maluach were responsible for the rest of the Suns' points that quarter – with Book scoring eight and Man Man chipping in four.

Maluach flashed some of his defensive potential on a play where he challenged and altered a layup attempt by Sandro Mamukelashvili and showed a quick second jump by immediately blocking a Jarred Vanderbilt layup attempt.

At the end of the first, the Suns found themselves down 33-24.

With Luka out to start the second, the Suns needed to take advantage of the non-Luka minutes – and, at first, it looked like they did. The Suns started the quarter with a Gillespie three to cut the lead to six, but that was the closest they would get (until the fourth). The Suns ended up losing the non-Luka minutes – letting Collin Sexton score eight points in the second. By the time Luka came back in the game with 4:56 left in the half, the Suns found themselves down 17.

That lead ballooned to 19, before the Suns started chipping away again. At the 3:36 mark, they were down 19. At that time, the story of the game was the difference from three (with the Lakers being +12) and from the free-throw line (+7). The Lakers also grabbed seven offensive rebounds in the second frame alone.

The only player showing any true effort on the boards for the Suns at this juncture was Jordan Goodwin — who was fouled on two separate occasions while trying to grab offensive rebounds off missed free throws.

Despite only having 10 points from Booker in the first half, the Suns were only down 10 at halftime.

The third quarter started a lot like the first. The Lakers were scoring and we could not. After the Lakers scored the first eight points, the Suns finally got some points from Devin Booker with 9:28 left. But it continued to be all Lakers from there.

Just like Collin Sexton stepped up for the Lakers in the second quarter, the third quarter belonged to Quentin Grimes. Grimes, who came in shooting 28% from three on the season, scored 11 in the quarter, including three 3-pointers. Luka also scored in double figures in the third quarter, chipping in 12.

In the third, the Suns shot 9-of-21 overall and 2-of-11 from three, while the Lakers shot 14-of-23 overall and 5-of-9 from three.

The fourth quarter started with little hope and a 24-point deficit. The Suns came out and promptly scored the first six points, and after the Lakers got the lead back to 22, Collin Gillespie hit back-to-back threes to cut the lead to 16 with 10 minutes left.

But then the offensive rebounds started coming back. Thybulle had a tip-in off a missed three, then on the next possession, Kessler had a put-back dunk on a missed layup by Thybulle. The Suns were down 19 with 8:15 left, and Koa Peat checked in – making it look like Jordan Ott had decided to pack it in.

But Peat checking in resulted in a furious comeback attempt that made a mundane afternoon into an exciting one.

Peat immediately impacted the game, fighting off Kessler on a Suns miss, which allowed the team to keep possession, then scoring on a strong shot over Kessler.

Collin Gillespie was also not ready for the game to be called, as he drew an and-1 on the next possession, to get the Suns within 14. This brought Luka and his 37 points back into the game. The first possession of Luka's return resulted in a turnover, and Gillespie missed a step-through jumper, but Peat was there for the tip-in. Suns down 12 with just over six minutes to go.

The Suns used a 10-1 run to find themselves down single digits with 5:02 to go. And they kept chipping away.

A Ryan Dunn three cut the lead to six with 4:37 left. Jake Laravia answers with a three of his own, but then Luke Kennard drops one to make it a six-point game again, but a missed three by Laravia followed by an offensive rebound and then a BANKED in three by Lavaria sealed the game for the Lakers.

An exciting comeback, but, ultimately, a 131-123 loss — and a loss that just further magnifies the obvious disconnect amongst the Suns starters. But still, Koa Peat…

The Suns hit the road immediately for an away matchup tomorrow against the Denver Nuggets.

#2661. Oliver Kahn fires back at Bayern over Musiala: "Loyalty is not a contractual obligation!"

Oliver Kahn has taken aim at Bayern Munich's handling of Jamal Musiala's health situation, delivering a strong message about loyalty, responsibility and player welfare. Following Uli Hoeneß's recent doubts about whether the 23-year-old can ever return to his previous level, the former Bayern CEO has offered a different perspective.

"Contractual loyalty is not loyalty. It is an obligation," Kahn wrote in a LinkedIn post. He argued that a club's true commitment only becomes apparent when a player can no longer deliver on the pitch.

"Clubs like to call themselves families. The problem starts when they talk about family as long as it costs nothing, and switch to talking numbers as soon as it becomes expensive," the 57-year-old added.

Kahn went even further, insisting that fulfilling a contract should not be celebrated as an extraordinary gesture of goodwill. "A club should not pretend that honouring the contract it signed itself is an act of particular humanity. The club did not just buy the performance. It also bought the risk."

The former goalkeeper also drew parallels with Manuel Neuer's serious leg injury in December 2022. Bayern publicly stood behind their captain before signing Yann Sommer just six weeks later.

"Both messages reach the player. But the second one is always heard much louder," Kahn concluded.

Musiala remains under contract until 2030, but has endured a difficult period with injuries and neurological issues. Bayern have stressed that continuing his playing career remains medically justifiable.

Joe Burrow is looking more and more like the NFL's MVP this season. And on Sunday night, the Cincinnati Bengals looked like a real threat to win a Super Bowl.

The Bengals' dismantling of the Pittsburgh Steelers seemed like a possible dawning of something special for Cincinnati. The Bengals were that good in a 38-18 win against the Steelers, who were 6-2 coming in. The Bengals are 7-2 and now have the lead spot in the AFC North race.

Burrow was nearly perfect, the Bengals' offensive line stymied the Steelers' pass rush and Cincinnati's defense shut down Pittsburgh. Burrow had 409 yards and four touchdowns, and could have had much more if the Steelers kept the game competitive.

It was a statement in the AFC North race. But after the way the Bengals played Sunday night in all phases, winning a division should be just the first part of Cincinnati's vision board. The team that a big national television audience watched Sunday night is capable of making a deep playoff run and maybe even finally winning it all.

The Bengals' mauling of the Steelers was unbelievable. It was the kind of domination you see in college, not the NFL.

When the Bengals took a 17-0 lead with 5:28 left in the second quarter, some of the stats were hard to believe. Burrow was 21-of-26 passing for 245 yards at that point, and Aaron Rodgers was 0-for-7. The Steelers as a team had 14. The Bengals had 18 first downs while the Steelers had one.

At halftime, Burrow had 302 yards and three touchdowns. He hit Dohnte Meyers for a 15-yard touchdown with nine seconds left in the half to give the Bengals a 24-3 lead. The Steelers were outgained 337-40 in the first half.

It is very hard to beat a professional team that thoroughly. Sometimes it can happen against an overmatched team or one that is heavily injured at the end of a lost season. This was a Steelers team that was tied for first place in the division coming in and was reasonably healthy.

The last three games make it clear. This season is all about managing expectations for fans of the Dallas Mavericks (7-7). But good grief.

The Mavericks dropped the second game of a back-to-back set in horrifying fashion, 131-94, in a Sunday matinee against the Boston Celtics (11-2) at TD Garden.

The unbridled optimism that came along with a surprise 7-4 start has been tempered, to say the least, after a pair of stinkers at the Minnesota Timberwolves and the Cleveland Cavaliers, followed by Sunday's scheduled loss, when the Mavs were again without star 34-year-old guard Kyrie Irving, due to injury management (rest).

The Celtics poured in three of their first four 3-point attempts to jump out to an 11-2 lead three minutes into the game, and the tone was set quickly. The Mavs didn't make their first shot from the field until Zaccharie Risacher hit a long jumper from the corner with 5:22 left in the first. The starting lineup of Cooper Flagg, Caleb Martin, Naji Marshall, Daniel Gafford and PJ Washington provided zero floor spacing on the offensive end.

And so, naturally, the Celtics' early lead swelled to 19-4 after Jordan Walsh went to the basket for six straight points on three straight possessions less than five minutes into the game. If Cooper Flagg isn't going out of his mind on offense, the roster as constructed for Sunday's game just doesn't stand a chance against the league's best teams.

Boston canned seven triples in the first quarter, while the Mavs shot an abysmal 2-of-18 from the field. The game was basically over as the Celtics led by an appalling 42-9 count after one. It goes without saying that the nine points were the lowest scoring output for the Mavs of the young 2026-27 season, but what was worse is that the team appeared to let it affect their effort on defense, as well.

The Mavericks woke up a little in the second quarter, but waking up after you're down 35 points is not worth a whole hell of a lot. A little 9-0 run late in the frame pulled the Mavs to within 59-34, but it seems laughable to even mention developments like that in the course of such a monumental shellacking.

Dallas turned the ball over 12 times in the first half to offset the team's five second-quarter 3-point makes, and Boston carried a lopsided 67-37 lead into the halftime break.

Flagg's early run of brilliance to start the season has hit a hard car crash of a stop. He shot a combined 11-of-31 in the two losses leading up to Sunday's game at Boston, and he followed that up by missing all three of his first-quarter shot attempts.

We see apex Flagg, as we've learned, when he plays next to competent guards, and that was simply not the case against the Celtics. The starting lineup at Boston featured exactly zero guards, and when Walter Clayton Jr. and Marcus Sasser entered halfway into the first, they offered little to no help on either end. Clayton came back in the second and scored eight points on two made 3-pointers, but the damage had been done at that point.

The Celtics' defense concentrated all their efforts into containing Flagg, because Flagg was the only viable source of offense left on Dallas' injury-riddled roster. He finally connected on his first field goal early in the second, on the low block through the foul of Payton Pritchard. But after two more 3-balls from the Celtics on the other end, the Celtics' lead had ballooned to 50-15 with nine minutes left in the first half.

There will be angst, and a certain amount of angst is warranted here, but circumstances aren't helping the 19-year-old star, either. He scored just five points in the first half and finished with 17 on 5-of-15 shooting in the loss.

Let's just get this out of the way and move on, shall we? Jayson Tatum torched the Mavericks for 21 of his game-high 32 points in the third quarter to lead way for the Celtics in the win. Derrick White added 16. Eight different Celtics made two or more 3-pointers, including Tatum, who put in five of them.

Risacher led the Mavericks with 18 off the bench on 8-of-9 shooting.

#2653. Celtics throttle Mavericks, 131-94, thanks to magnificent 42-9 1st quarter

Some NBA games are won late in the fourth quarter, with dramatic twists and turns in the final seconds and elite shotmaking from the game's brightest stars.

Sunday was not one of those games. This one was over before many fans settled into their seats, as the Celtics led by 33 through 1 en route to a dominant 131-94 victory at TD Garden.

"We were playing well, forcing them into shots we want them to take, and they missed some shots," said Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla.

Boston (11-2) has now won six straight, including four by 20 or more, and is still in first place in the Eastern Conference. Dallas (7-7), playing without Kyrie Irving (knee) on the second night of a back to back, looked outmatched in every facet early.

Jayson Tatum led the way with 32 points (11-of-18 shooting), 6 rebounds and 6 assists. Boston shot 51 percent as a team, leaving no doubt and improving to 6-0 at home on the season.

The Celtics absolutely dominated the first quarter, building a 42-9 advantage through 1 with a truly spectacular performance. Yes, it was the largest lead after the first quarter in franchise history. It felt like it, too.

Boston shot 59 percent from the floor and 54 percent from 3, while Dallas was at 11 percent from the field and 0 percent from distance. The Celtics racked up 14 points in the paint, compared to 2 for the Mavericks, and won the rebounding battle, 16-10.

Boston could do no wrong. Dallas could do no right.

"We tried to shrink the floor as much as possible and cause havoc," said Celtics wing Jordan Walsh.

Walsh played with conviction and purpose and helped set the tone early, and Derrick White (16 points) found a rhythm early to help extend the lead. Seemingly every shot the Celtics threw up went in, as the action resembled a varsity team scrimmaging a junior varsity team.

The Mavericks found their footing in the second quarter and chipped away, but the Celtics preserved a 67-37 lead heading into halftime following a relatively even second quarter.

"Obviously it's easy to really bring it when it's a close game, or things like that," Tatum said. "Just trying to challenge our mindset of we're up 25 to 30, can you try to put the game away? I think we did a really good job of that today."

Tatum, Pritchard and White continued to flourish, and Sam Hauser provided strong minutes off the bench. Zaccharie Risacher (18 points) paced Dallas with 9 in the half, but Cooper Flagg (17) struggled and the Mavericks turned it over six more times in the quarter.

Eleven players saw the floor for Boston and nine scored, led by White with 11.

The Celtics kept their target practice going in the third quarter, as Paul George and Walsh hit back-to-back corner 3's to push the margin to 34. Neemias Queta added one of his own from the other corner to improve to 4 of 5 from distance on the season.

"His growth and his role has gone kind of under the radar," Mazzulla said of Queta. "He's more important than just with defense. He's important in the locker room, he's important on the offensive end. He continues to get better and better. It's easy to overlook it because of how easy he makes it."

Flagg got going in the third, but Tatum continued to cook and kept the lead hovering around 30 most of the way.

Tatum drilled a step-back 3 with 4.3 seconds left to make it 104-71 through three. He finished the quarter with 21 and continued to look like pre-injury Tatum.

The Celtics started the fourth with Baylor Scheierman, Devin Carter, Ron Harper Jr., Hugo González and Luka Garza, and they continued to play the brand of basketball that got Boston to that point.

Harper Jr. converted inside, Scheierman and Harper Jr. swished consecutive 3's and Garza delivered inside to push it to 40, 117-77, with 8:58 to go.

"The start of the fourth quarter, we made them call the first timeout," Mazzulla said.

Gino Time came with 2:51 remaining and the Celtics up 36. The win streak is alive, and the Celtics are looking very much like contenders.

#2652. Cowboys’ Brian Schottenheimer Rips’Atrocious’ Defense

The Dallas Cowboys had one of the worst defensive games in the history of the franchise on Sunday against a high-powered 49ers attack, and while there were some encouraging signs with the way the team hung in and fought back against the league's best team, the fact that the defense yielded 584 yards of offense seemed to break coach Brian Schottenheimer's ability to level-headed and cool, as he usually is in press conferences, no matter the result. The Cowboys lost, 46-40, and that would not be such a bad result, except that the game was littered with poor tackling and enormous chunk plays by the 49ers that clearly raised Schottenheimer's blood pressure several points.

When he met with Cowboys reporters after the game, Schottenheimer was not shy about pointing to the disappointment he had in coordinator Christian Parker's defense.

Schottenheimer frequently takes blame himself when things go wrong for the Cowboys. Not on Sunday.

Here's what he said in full: "The second half was unacceptable. The tackling was atrocious. And we are going to do a deep dive on the film and see why. You can't give up three explosive plays of over 65 yards for touchdowns and expect to win in this league. Do a deep dive on the film but totally unacceptable defense in that second half."

He was asked about whether he thinks Parker can get the defense solved, and Schottenheimer did not give a wholeheartedly positive response: "We have to look at it. We are gonna watch a lot of film because there are a lot of things I have to figure out. I have never been around a situation like this where the defense was that poor in the second half. We rushed the passer well, got the five sacks …

"But what is killing us is missed tackles and explosive players. Go back to Indianapolis last week. We play good defense, give up a 65-yard touchdown. Play good defense, give up a 70-yard touchdown. Can't do that."

And yet, the Cowboys did. And the coach was not happy.

After the performance against the Steelers, they may want to make that alternate kit permanent.

Quarterback Joe Burrow and receiver Ja'Marr Chase were stellar on Sunday night, with Cincinnati defeating division-rival Pittsburgh 38-18.

In just the first half, Burrow had 302 yards and three touchdowns before finishing the contest 35-of-44 for 409 yards with four TDs. Joe Flacco came in for mop-up duty midway through the final period.

The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions, and would have made it all five if Evan McPherson had hit his 43-yard field goal attempt that sailed wide right. That was McPherson's first missed kick of the season.

But McPherson had opened the scoring with a 24-yard field goal to cap the opening drive. Drew Sample had a 3-yard TD catch, Chase Brown had a 2-yard score, and Dohnte Meyers had a 15-yard touchdown reception to give the Bengals a 24-3 halftime lead.

Brown caught his second touchdown in the third quarter to make it 31-3. And Samaje Perine closed the Bengals' scoring with his 1-yard touchdown run with 10:08 left in the fourth quarter.

#2648. Mavericks score just 9 points in opening quarter during historic loss to Jayson Tatum, Celtics

The Dallas Mavericks got out to a horrific and historically bad start on Sunday night at TD Garden.

The Boston Celtics rolled to a 42-9 lead in the opening quarter. That marked Boston's largest lead at the end of the first period in franchise history.

It gets even worse for the Mavericks. The Celtics' 42-9 scoring margin was the best from any team in the league in any quarter since 1987, when the Los Angeles Lakers outscored the Sacramento Kings 40-4 in the first quarter, according to ESPN. It was also the third-best mark by a team in a quarter in the shot-clock era, which started back in 1954.

Remarkably, it wasn't the Mavericks' worst quarter in franchise history. They managed just two points in a quarter in a game against the Los Angeles Lakers in 1997.

On Sunday, the Mavericks made just two of their first 18 field-goal attempts in the opening quarter, and went a brutal 0 of 8 from behind the arc. Of their nine points in the opening frame, five of them came from the free-throw line.

"I didn't feel like we were turning it over early," Mavericks coach Dusty May said, via the Dallas Morning News' Mike Curtis. "I felt like we had some decent looks. We didn't convert them. I'd have to go back and look at the film for any specifics of why we weren't able to score."

And while things did get better for the Mavericks, it was far too late to make a difference. The Celtics took a 30-point lead into the locker room at halftime, and then rolled to the 131-94 victory.

Jayson Tatum led Boston with 32 points, 6 rebounds and 6 assists while shooting 11 of 18 from the field in the win. Derrick White added 16 points, and Baylor Scheierman finished with 12 points and five rebounds off the bench. Boston shot 51% from the field as a team and forced 17 turnovers.

The Celtics are now 11-2 on the season. They have won six straight, too, and hold a slight lead over the Philadelphia 76ers in the Eastern Conference standings.

Zaccharie Risacher led the Mavericks with 18 points off the bench after he went 8 of 9 from the field. Cooper Flagg finished with 17 points, and Walter Clayton added 13 points. The Mavericks were coming off a loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers in Ohio on Saturday night.

They have now lost three in a row and sit at 7-7 on the season. Thankfully, after a rough three-game road trip capped by a truly bad outing on Sunday, Flagg and the Mavericks will have three days to recover. They'll host the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday night.
