#2644. Utah Jazz lose heartbreaking game against San Antonio Spurs

The Jazz welcomed the red-hot San Antonio Spurs to the Delta Center on Sunday afternoon, hoping to snap an 11-game losing streak. Unfortunately for Utah, the Spurs entered the game riding an 11-game winning streak of their own. Polar opposites. San Antonio pulled away in the final minutes, winning 110-102.

This is about as drastic of a matchup as you'll see in the NBA, but the Jazz came out hot, looking to build on the momentum they established against another one of the league's best teams, the Houston Rockets, who they narrowly lost to just a few days ago.

The Jazz put up 33 points in the first quarter, led by Mo Bamba, who scored 10. Speaking of Bamba, what an incredible performance he put together. While the Jazz ended up losing, this will forever be remembered as the Mo Bamba game.

Bamba finished with 26 points, five rebounds, four assists and three combined steals and blocks, highlighted by shooting a perfect 6-for-6 from 3-point range. The breakout game took a while for Bamba, but it finally happened.

The Jazz held a 10-point lead with just under two minutes remaining in the first quarter. The second quarter was a response from the Spurs, who eventually built a 10-point lead with nine minutes remaining in the third.

It looked as if the red-hot Spurs were going to run away with their 12th straight win.

Peterson went on to score eight straight points, making it look easy. He also could've easily earned a few trips to the free-throw line, yet he finished with zero attempts. As a team, the Jazz attempted just six free throws compared to San Antonio's 20.

It wasn't Peterson's best night, yet he still managed to demonstrate the talent that could lead him to receiving MVP votes someday. If a bad night for Peterson consists of 17 points, five rebounds, four assists and three combined steals and blocks, then goodness, everyone else is in trouble.

His efficiency was actually solid until the fourth quarter, when he simply couldn't get a shot to fall, going 0-for-5 in the final period. Several of his attempts came up short, leading me to wonder whether all the minutes Peterson has played are starting to wear him down just a little.

Peterson will be just fine, and he doesn't even turn 20 until January.

Keyonte George had another rough night, shooting under 30% from the field for the second time since returning from his ankle sprain. His shot selection was questionable at times, and that was the biggest difference between Peterson and George tonight. Neither was particularly efficient, but Peterson was generating good looks while George often found himself forcing difficult shots.

Isaiah Collier and Kyle Filipowski both received DNPs from head coach Will Hardy.

Josh Green and Josh Okogie both made positive contributions, with Green finishing at plus-4 and Okogie at plus-2. Svi Mykhailiuk, who has received plenty of criticism for his play, deserves some credit tonight after going 2-for-3 from beyond the arc and finishing with a team-high plus-15.

The Jazz are now a league-worst 1-13, having lost 12 consecutive games.

I know the injuries have been crazy. George missed the Miami game, and with a good performance from him in that matchup, Utah probably comes away with a win.

We also haven't seen projected starter Jusuf Nurkić yet, although he was going through some warmups before Sunday's game. Getting Nurkić back will help, but it won't solve everything. Don't expect him to shoot 6-for-6 from deep and score 26 points like Bamba did today.

Nobody can argue that missing two All-Star-caliber players isn't having a massive impact on this Jazz team right now. Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen are clearly missed.

That being said, there's still at least a month before Markkanen returns and probably a month and a half, minimum, before Jackson is back.

This current group has to figure something out. Otherwise, when the cavalry finally arrives, it might not matter.

And don't forget, Jaxson Hayes also missed today's game.

Will Hardy has to figure things out as soon as possible. At this point, it's not even about making the playoffs or the play-in tournament. It's about showing that he's capable of winning basketball games.

Right now, that's literally something the Jazz cannot do.

If one Dejounte Murray shot goes differently, the Jazz are sitting at 0-14.

I'm not sold on Hardy right now. These weird two-man games he runs, which seemingly always result in a contested jump shot during the final seconds of the shot clock, continue to infuriate and confuse me.

On the other side, Dylan Harper dominated the Jazz in the fourth quarter. Stephon Castle mostly had his way as well, using his strength to overpower Peterson on a few occasions.

Victor Wembanyama was mostly slowed down in the second half. After posting 21 points in the first half, he managed just five in the second. For a player of his stature, you'll take that.

The Jazz wasted an incredible performance from Bamba today. They played well enough to win, but for what feels like the hundredth time this season, Utah was unable to close out a game when it mattered most.

The young Jazz will search for answers Tuesday when they take on a Los Angeles Clippers team with just two wins of its own. Tipoff is scheduled for 9 p.m. MST.

#2643. Sunday Night Football: Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase torch Steelers in 38-18 Bengals victory

The Bengals wanted to create a special “white out” environment for Sunday’s game, with the home team wearing its “White Bengal” uniform and helmet.

After the performance against the Steelers, they may want to make that alternate kit permanent.

Quarterback Joe Burrow and receiver Ja’Marr Chase were stellar on Sunday night, with Cincinnati defeating division-rival Pittsburgh 38-18.

In just the first half, Burrow had 302 yards and three touchdowns before finishing the contest 35-of-44 for 409 yards with four TDs. Joe Flacco came in for mop-up duty midway through the final period.

Burrow also tied Peyton Manning’s record streak of five consecutive games of at least four touchdowns.

As he often is, Chase was Burrow’s favorite target, catching 11 passes for 231 yards. While Chase didn’t have a touchdown himself, he caught deep bombs of 53 and 43 yards that helped set up scores.

It was the third-highest output of Chase’s career and the fourth time he’s gone over 200 yards in a regular-season game.

The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions, and would have made it all five if Evan McPherson had hit his 43-yard field goal attempt that sailed wide right. That was McPherson’s first missed kick of the season.

But McPherson had opened the scoring with a 24-yard field goal to cap the opening drive. Drew Sample had a 3-yard TD catch, Chase Brown had a 2-yard score, and Dohnte Meyers had a 15-yard touchdown reception to give the Bengals a 24-3 halftime lead.

Brown caught his second touchdown in the third quarter to make it 31-3. And Samaje Perine closed the Bengals’ scoring with his 1-yard touchdown run with 10:08 left in the fourth quarter.

As well as Cincinnati’s offense played, the defense may have been better. Aaron Rodgers started the contest 0-of-8 passing, with his first completion not coming until there was 4:31 left in the second quarter.

Pittsburgh had just four first downs and 40 total yards at halftime.

Rodgers ended the night 15-of-29 for 143 yards with two touchdowns, both of which came in the fourth quarter after the game was out of reach. Rodgers was also sacked three times.

With the win, the Bengals are now 7-2 on the season and have sole possession of first place in the AFC North. They will have an extra day to prepare, as they’ll face the Commanders next Monday night.

The Steelers fall to 6-3 and will be on the road to face the Eagles next Sunday afternoon.

#2641. Not a cold streak; the Utah Jazz are historically bad

When the buzzer sounded on San Antonio's 110-102 win in Salt Lake City, the reigning Western Conference champions tallied their 12th consecutive win, pushing their record to an NBA-leading 12-2. The Utah Jazz, losers of Sunday's Delta Center duel, likewise extended an active streak of 12 games. 12 losses in a row.

12 straight losses are tied for the second-longest losing streak in franchise history, but that's not even the worst part of this all.

This is only the second time the Jazz have started a season 1-13. The first time? The Jazz played their home games in New Orleans, Louisiana, and were playing their very first season as an NBA franchise. That 1974-75 team opened the season with a 1-16 record and fired head coach Scotty Robertson following their 14th loss.

This Utah Jazz team isn't just bad — they're historically bad.

Yes, this year's team has been playing at a deficit when it comes to injuries. They would have likely picked up a few more wins to this point were Jaren Jackson Jr., Jusuf Nurkic, and Lauri Markkanen not seated courtside, modeling the Polo Fall 2026 line at the end of the bench. Even so, Utah's foundation is riddled with cracks and is nowhere near the level of a playoff participant.

Undersized at the wing, Utah is consistently out-physicaled and outdone athletically against every team they've faced.

It's not all bad news, though. The Jazz's stars and veterans are all expected to return in a month or so, and they have already faced each of the Western Conference's top-six teams. After facing this slate in the early season, Utah's schedule will only get easier:

Even at full strength, Utah couldn't have reasonably expected to escape that gauntlet with a winning record.

The biggest issue facing the Jazz right now isn't injuries. It isn't inexperience. It isn't even personnel. The Jazz simply don't know how to win — they've never tried before.

It's a team that has grown accustomed to losing for the last four years, and those habits have reappeared night after night.

They took San Antonio and New Orleans into overtime, only to concede a 12-0 run in each of those additional five-minute periods. They fumbled away a 10-point third-quarter lead against Houston but clawed back to within one point at the 2:46 mark, only to relinquish a 2-8 run in crunch time. Down just one point against Memphis with one minute remaining, Utah failed to score again. Behind LA by one point with three minutes to go, the Jazz still couldn't seal the deal with JJJ and Markkanen active.

They've put themself in a position to win several times, but only once did they hold on to win.

How's this for glass-half-empty: Utah is one Dejounte Murray jumper away from being 0-14.

The Jazz front office continues to back Will Hardy as head coach, determined to support the man who patiently endured four years of non-competitive basketball to lead Utah back into the playoffs when the time is right. Just as Utah's roster is learning how to win in a competitive NBA, Hardy's baptism by fire has likewise left him a bit seared.

Now is not the time to take drastic measures — still 68 games to go in the season — but Utah's issues are buried much deeper than a string of bad luck.

Calvin Barrett is the Associate Editor for SLC Dunk and a Utah Jazz columnist for the Standard-Examiner. Originally from Springville, Utah, he currently writes from his desk in Japan.

#2639. The Steelers and Bengals final score has never happened before in NFL history

On Sunday, we saw two scores that have never happened in the history of the NFL. On Sunday afternoon, the Dallas Cowboys and San Francisco 49ers were the 1099th and on Sunday night, the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers played to the 1100th.

It's the second time this season we've had two Scorigamis in one weekend.

When we get a new final score in the NFL, it's called Scorigami. Normally when we get a Scorigami it's because a team scores an absolute boatload of points and often something weird happens, usually with two-point conversions. We got both on Sunday with the Bengals and Steelers.

The Bengals took a big lead on Pittsburgh in the fourth quarter, but it was a pretty typical 28-point, four-touchdown lead. Nothing weird. Then the Pittsburgh Steelers scored a touchdown and went for two. If turned a three-touchdown deficit into a… three-touchdown deficit. Really not sure when the Steelers chose to do it. That 31-11 score would have been a Scorigami, too.

After the Bengals scored to make it 38-11, that would not have been a Scorigami but the Steelers scored one more time to make it 38-18. That threaded the needle. The only 38-point winners that haven't hit now are 38-2 and 38-4.

Our friends at Secret Base have done extensive work on Scorigami. If you want to see it, it is fascinating.

This is the fifth Scorigami of the 2026 NFL season.

September 13: Chicago Bears 59, Carolina Panthers 37

#2638. Germany dominate Serbia in rain-soaked Nations League clash

Germany have made a good start to the last Nations League phase in 2026, beating Serbia 3-1 in a rain-soaked contest. Goals from Wirtz and debutant Gruda mean that Germany still have the chance to top their Nations League group.

The unusual behind-closed-doors atmosphere has seen selected groups of children under 15 admitted alongside teachers and football coaches following UEFA sanctions against Serbia for discrimination. However, the game still delivered on the entertainment front.

Jürgen Klopp's side needed just two minutes to break the deadlock, with Kai Havertz getting on the end of a corner before his attempt was deflected into the net by Srdan Babić for an own goal.

Germany doubled their advantage in the 14th minute following a brilliant, Klopp-esque pressing sequence. Aleksandar Pavlović played a superb through ball to Havertz, whose effort was denied by goalkeeper Vanja Milinković-Savić. Florian Wirtz reacted quickest to the rebound and calmly chipped the ball into the net.

Germany dominated the remainder of the first half, enjoying 75% possession and completing 94% of their passes. Their superiority continued after the break, with Brajan Gruda capping a fantastic solo run with a clinical finish in the 50th minute to make it 3-0.

Serbia responded just six minutes later. Babić made amends for his earlier own goal by reacting quickest after Stefan Gudelj's header from a free kick was saved, converting the rebound to give the hosts a lifeline.

Joshua Kimmich thought he had restored Germany's three-goal advantage shortly afterwards with a powerful low strike from the edge of the box. However, the goal was correctly ruled out due to Kai Havertz's passive offside position.

Derry Scherhant, one of Germany's standout performers under Klopp so far, had enjoyed a relatively quiet evening but came close to scoring in the 70th minute. After cutting inside from the left, his effort beat the goalkeeper but struck the woodwork.

Serbia substitute Aleksandar Mitrović also came close to scoring, but Marc-André ter Stegen stood firm to keep his effort out. Things then went from bad to worse for the hosts as Vanja Dragojevic received a straight red card for a dangerous challenge on Germany captain Joshua Kimmich, accidentally standing on his ankle.

Dragojević was not the only Serbian to leave the pitch early. Substitute Andrija Zivković also saw red after picking up two yellow cards in quick succession following an animated exchange with the referee shortly before full-time.

Klopp used the opportunity to introduce several other Bundesliga names, including Niclas Füllkrug, Felix Nmecha and Said El Mala. However, none managed to make a significant impact during their limited time on the pitch. They could get another opportunity when Germany face the Netherlands on Monday.

The match also marked a historic first for Germany, with Kimmich and Pavlović starting together as a double pivot for the first time. The partnership showed plenty of promise and could become a regular feature under Klopp.

Finally, it was also Germany's last appearance in their long-standing partnership with Adidas. Given the convincing performance, it was certainly a fitting farewell.

#2637. Stats Rundown: 3 numbers to know from the Mavericks’ 131-94 loss at the Boston Celtics

The Dallas Mavericks lost in embarrassing fashion, 131-94 to the Boston Celtics Sunday night in Boston. This is the Mavericks third loss in a row to drop the team back to .500 at 7-7, with all three losses being fairly dispiriting.

It started awful and never got better, with the Mavericks trailing by a double-take-inducing 33 points at the end of the first quarter. The Mavericks had zero gumption or energy to start the game, after losing a game Saturday night to a Cleveland team with zero of their starters active.

Zaccharie Risacher led the Mavericks with 18 points. Jayson Tatum led Boston and all scorers with 32, as the Celtics shot over 50 percent from the field and over 40 percent from three.

It's early, but the Mavericks have reached their first crisis point of the season — if they want to be the surprise playoff team people thought after the team started 7-4, the turnaround has to happen quickly.

The Mavericks didn't shoot the ball poorly, considering their personnel, but even with 14 made threes, the Celtics still made nine more three pointers. It was a gap too wide to overcome.

Boston is a machine, and the Mavericks couldn't keep up. Dallas' defense features a lot of forwards and bigs, but the footspeed and defensive talent on the perimeter waxes and wanes — Dallas can recover with splashy defensive plays and deflections, but the team is prone to blow-bys since the Mavericks don't have much point-of-attack defense. The Celtics got the Mavericks into rotation early and Dallas never recovered.

After a meteroic start to the season, Flagg is officially in a slump. He was 5-of-15 against the Celtics, including 2-of-6 from three. Flagg has been under 40 percent from the field in four of the eight games he's played in November, and been under 45 percent in six of the eight. He's now shooting just 42 percent in November, and 26 percent from three.

Dallas' lineup did him no favors tonight, as Dusty May rolled out the Jason Kidd/Nico Harrison special from a year ago, with Flagg running point next to four non-shooting threats in PJ Washington, Caleb Martin, Naji Marshall, and Daniel Gafford. Washington and Martin have solid percentages this season, but they don't warp the defense with their spacing, especially without a lead guard to disrupt the defense. Flagg was seeing two, three, and even four bodies in front of him inside the three point line on just about every drive.

This is a problem for the Mavericks. Flagg is obviously a special talent, but the apex version of him is usually unlocked when next to a competent lead guard that can get downhill. We saw this last season and we've seen it again this season, as Dallas has played very well with Kyrie Irving and Flagg on the floor together. This is no knock on Flagg, but playing him without a credible guard talent next to him is like trying to win a game with one arm tied behind your back.

Unfortunately Dallas hasn't prioritized a lead guard in the last two offseasons. Dallas used the ninth overall pick in this summer's draft for Morez Johnson Jr., another big and then brought in another big in Santi Aldama via trade. Dallas' only guard moves were a smaller move for end-of-the-bench prospect Marcus Sasser, who's shown flashes, and using a late first-rounder for Sergio de Larrea, who is currently injured. Walter Clayton Jr. joined the team a week before the season started on a two-way contract and was almost immediately the team's backup point guard. The Dallas guard rotation is bleak, and especially so when guys like de Larrea and Max Christie are injured.

Bottom line: the Mavericks have to prioritize the guard position over the course of the next 18 months, whether that's at the upcoming trade deadline, next summer's draft, or the ensuing offseason. It's going to hold this whole thing back until it's resolved.

It says a lot about how bad Dallas is as a defensive rebounding team when the Celtics can get 18 offensive boards on a night where they were shooting the leather off the ball. There weren't a lot of misses for the Celtics to go get, and yet they still found themselves with a sizable offensive rebounding advantage (18-11).

Dallas cannot be this big of a team and still fail to rebound the ball consistently. It's just an untenable combination. If the Mavericks want to be a big, lengthy, athletic team, then they have to play like it. It does the team no good to be this big as a roster and this bad at rebounding. The trickle down effects are apparent. Nothing else to say, except the Mavericks just have to be better.

Luka Dončić continues to dominate as a scorer this season, but the Los Angeles Lakers will have to find a way to support their star player.

Lakers coach JJ Redick referred to Dončić as one of the league's best scorers before a game against the Phoenix Suns on Sunday, a sentiment shared by Giannis Antetokounmpo of the Miami Heat earlier this month.

Dončić nearly produced a double-double with 43 points on 13-of-28 shooting and nine assists for Los Angeles in the 131-123 road victory, living up to his coach's remarks.

Despite having one of the best records in the league (12-2), the third-year coach had other remarks and expectations for his team; he used the recent three-day break to share a 21-page analytics presentation with his players to serve as an internal audit on both offense and defense.

"A lot of good things and a lot of things to clean up," Lakers forward Ziaire Williams told reporters on Nov. 13. "Being first in the (Western Conference), with the stuff that they showed us, you would think we were almost last."

It is the Lakers' eighth straight win, with the last four coming on the road, but one of those aspects of the game that needs to be cleaned up is apparent.

Dončić and Austin Reaves, who was out Sunday due to injury, have proven they can win games together and can also take on a role as the high-scoring threat with the other out of the lineup.

Beyond the two stars, there's some inconsistency with the team's depth to help complement that scoring and allow its superstars an opportunity to rest.

Dončić ushered the Lakers to a quick start once again this season, scoring eight of the team's first 10 unanswered points. He finished the first quarter with 20 of the team's 33 points in the first quarter.

"We're working too hard and we're playing too hard to build these leads," Redick said during the postgame press conference on Sunday. "It's a disservice to each other to take your foot off the gas."

Los Angeles has held the lead in 76.8% of the game time this season, which is the best in the NBA, according to the Lakers. The team also has displayed its offensive dominance during its recent four-game stretch, having led for 92% of the game time.

The Lakers went wire-to-wire on Sunday, leading by as many as 31 points during the game, but allowed the Suns to battle back into the game with 43 points in the final frame.

"I wasn't planning to play in the fourth quarter," Dončić told reporters after the game. "We got to get better at that. I know we won eight in a row, but we got to get better at that.

"Once we get up, we got to stay there. We got to work on that."

Dončić gave credit to the Suns, who played aggressively while Los Angeles started the fourth quarter "a little bit sloppy."

Redick has stated multiple times this week that the Lakers' desire is to work toward being a top 10 defense in the NBA. The Lakers rank near the middle of the pack in terms of defensive rating, allowing close to 114 points per game.

After the game, Redick recalled a moment that could be featured in his next audit for the defense.

"We did a lot of good things through three quarters," Redick explained on Sunday. "... In the fourth, when (the Suns) are walking it up and we don't even talk and get matched up.

"They hit wide-open 3s and get going. You just can't allow that. You have to play for 48 minutes. We are going to need our defense to win us games."

The Lakers will have another chance to work toward Redick's defensive expectations against the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday, Nov. 17 at 11 p.m. ET (8 p.m. PT).

#2632. As Vikings flash complementary football 'for one of the first times' this year in Kirk Cousins' return, Fernando Mendoza sums up Raiders debut: 'It's good to get punched in the face'

Facing third-and-23 in the first quarter, Kirk Cousins dropped back.

His offensive line was slowing the Packers' rushers threatening from his left.

Second-year undrafted free-agent receiver Myles Price was crossing the field from his right.

So Cousins wound up and hit Price on a crosser, Price bouncing off Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse and racing the 14 remaining yards to the end zone.

The 38-yard touchdown marked the first touchdown reception of Price's career and the first in Cousins' return to the Vikings after a Tuesday trade from the Las Vegas Raiders made him the first quarterback to start for two different teams in back-to-back weeks, per Fox.

The timing that play required? The poise in the pocket just four days after Cousins had arrived at the Vikings' practice facility wondering what code he needed to input to enter the building?

"That's probably the [touchdown] that you're thinking, 'Is there enough time on task … ?'" head coach Kevin O'Connell said after the Vikings beat the Packers, 30-10. "We're kind of in a four-by-one look right there. They're dropping somebody in. Myles runs right into the hook area kind of behind there and you've got to get that ball thrown with pretty elite timing and you're really throwing it into a spot with some trust that Myles is going to go get it because inevitably the corner may fall off.

Improving to 7-2, the Vikings showed their first glimpse of what a high-ceiling offense might look like beside one of the best defenses in the league. Brian Flores' unit was the star of the show yet again, sacking Jordan Love eight times and securing four takeaways. The Vikings contained the Packers to 10 points and 220 yards just one week after Green Bay embarrassed the Patriots to the tune of 45 points and 478 yards.

Add in 312 yards and 30 points on offense after the Vikings averaged 266.8 and 18.3 before Cousins' arrival?

"Obviously there's a lot to build off of from this," O'Connell said. But "for one of the first times this year, I thought we played complementary football."

Expect the ceiling only to rise as Cousins acclimates to his reunion with a team that deemed the remainder of his season worth a third-round pick and a $10 million salary hit.

And the Raiders team that parted with Cousins?

Rookie first overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza started off strongly before the No. 1-ranked Seahawks defense stifled the Raiders in the second half of a 21-13 loss. Mendoza spoke to the opportunity the unraveling could provide.

"It's good to get punched in the face, because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game and as a future hopeful leader of this offense …" Mendoza said. "There's a lot of things I need to improve on in that field, and I'm excited to watch the film and get back to work."

Fernando Mendoza felt the Seahawks' heat in his first NFL start this season.

When former Dallas Cowboys head coach Jason Garrett suggested a recipe to onboard Mendoza last week, it seemed ideal but unrealistic.

"Quiet the game down for him, try to get the running game going early, high-percentage throws early, move the quarterback," Garrett said Wednesday on an NBC conference call. "Try to get him to be 5-for-5 [passing] before he even thinks about it to get into the flow of the game."

As an aspiration, that sounded great. But was a Raiders team that ranked among the league's worst in both rushing and defense really going to be able to support a new quarterback that way? How much could the passing game withstand the loss of Cousins, who ranked fifth in passing yards and 11th in passer rating when he left for Minnesota?

Credit Mendoza and Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak's early game plan: Mendoza not only started 5-for-5 against Seattle; he completed seven straight passes before his first incompletion. Las Vegas' early offense was balanced and steady, Mendoza operating from under center and running bootlegs off play action.

During the first half, Las Vegas kept Seattle's defense honest: Mendoza scrambled for a yard on third-and-1 to keep his first drive alive and later for 8 yards on third-and-5 near first quarter's end. And as if in ode to his fourth-and-4 national championship highlight, Mendoza tucked and ran for a 10-yard touchdown to give the Raiders an early 7-0 lead.

"Got to give the Raiders a lot of credit in the first half," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said afterward. "I thought they had a good plan, and they made it challenging for us in the first half. But our guys did a great job adjusting and sticking together and finding a way to win in the end."

The Seahawks' adjustments, paired with the loss of two-time Pro Bowl tight end Brock Bowers to an ankle injury, derailed a promising start.

With the help of defensive-back blitzes that Macdonald said resulted from in-game looks, the Seahawks sacked Mendoza four times in the second half after just two in the first. Seattle's pressure disrupted the timing of Mendoza's passing game and shuttered the Raiders' run game: After converting 7-of-10 third-down attempts in the first half, Las Vegas went 0-for-7 in the second half. The Raiders followed up a 62-yard rushing performance in the first half with just 3 net yards in the second. Ten first downs in the first half preceded just two across quarters three and four.

And after Mendoza opened the game 11-of-13 for 90 yards passing, in addition to notching the rushing touchdown, before halftime — he managed to complete just 6-of-16 attempts for 53 yards and no touchdowns in the second half.

"It just felt like such a weird game," Raiders tight end Michael Mayer said. "I don't really know how to describe it. Felt like we started out pretty good, and then I really don't know what happened after that."

Kubiak and Mendoza each said they hold themselves to higher standards than they reached in the loss.

"There was a lot of sacks there," Mendoza said. "We should have had half as many if not even less than that. So I need to mature as a quarterback, throw the ball away, throw more accurate balls on third down and making sure we can move the chains to give our defense time to recuperate on the sideline and to really get it going in the second half."

The Vikings and Raiders' playoff hopes are trending in different directions.

Minnesota's chances of advancing to the postseason improved to 90% with its Sunday win, per Next Gen Stats, even as it sits in second place in a crowded NFC North. The Raiders' chances fell to 10% after their loss, their 4-6 record paired with their remaining schedule projecting worse chances than also-currently-out-of-it AFC contenders in the New England Patriots, Baltimore Ravens and Houston Texans.

A similarity between the two teams whose fates will be tied this season by their shared Cousins custody: the expectation of evolution as the offensive cast settles into its roles.

In Minnesota, Cousins reunited with a handful of teammates including receiver Justin Jefferson, whom he said "felt like old times watching Justin do what he just did." But plenty of teammates, and parts of the Vikings' playbook like the run concepts assistant head coach Frank Smith implemented this season, remain new. Cousins is no stranger to new play-callers: "I've changed coordinators 11 times," he said after the game. But there were times during his quick turnaround week when Cousins said he told O'Connell and Co., "You know what, I would be more comfortable doing this."

"You can't just roll the ball out there and ask the quarterback to have all the answers while they're still digesting their in-flight meal from when they came here," O'Connell said.

With just two full-speed practices after Cousins' arrival, O'Connell said he did not think Cousins took a full-speed rep of the double-pump 20-yard touchdown on which he hit Gavin Bartholomew in the fourth quarter.

"I think it was just either a walkthrough or maybe a jog or something, but it looked the way it's supposed to look…" O'Connell said. "Kirk just couldn't have executed better."

Kubiak, meanwhile, was kicking himself for some decisions he implemented with Mendoza. Those rollouts that worked for Mendoza in the first half? "Should have done more of that for sure," Kubiak said of shifting the plan.

The Raiders' resilience to losing Bowers, whose 676 yards and six touchdowns receiving both lead Las Vegas?

"I thought overall when we lost Brock we definitely saw a big change in production," Kubiak said. "So I look at myself. I have to do a much better job of moving the ball and spreading the ball around. …

"Overall, we've got to play better. We've got to support him better."

With just one game down, and a schedule that will lighten in December, the Raiders will have more chances. Perhaps Cousins' summation of his day applies to both teams — as well as to how NFL history will ultimately remember this rare in-season trade of a starting quarterback.

"There's just so much football ahead," Cousins said, "and this story is going to get written much later than now."

#2631. Wales must look to back up All Blacks win - Tandy

Wales head coach Steve Tandy has challenged his side to back up their wonderful win against New Zealand when they host Australia next weekend.

After beating the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years with the 35-28 win at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Wales face the final game of the Nations Championship - before the play-offs - against the Wallabies on Saturday evening (20:10 BST).

Tandy says Wales will attempt not to dwell on what they achieved on Saturday against New Zealand as they aim for a third successive home win.

"We have to keep going and we've got a massive game against Australia next weekend," said Tandy.

"It's going to be a different kind of test for us after we have had back-to-back home wins.

"We've gone up another notch or another couple of levels, so it's important we back that up. It's about making sure when we come in that we're ready to work."

After defeat to England, Australia lost 15-12 against Scotland on Sunday, a result which leaves Wales fifth in the northern hemisphere table.

Wales are behind behind Gregor Townsend's side on points difference with Scotland finishing their campaign against Japan.

Tandy's side have won three out of five games in the Nations Championship against Fiji, Japan and New Zealand with defeats in the summer against Argentina and South Africa.

Captain Dewi Lake has highlighted what has changed for this campaign to enable Wales to defeat New Zealand and rise one place in the world rankings to ninth.

"Our skills are better and I think we're a better team which is credit to Steve and his coaches," said Lake.

"I think the belief is also different and the mindset has shifted.

"We've spoken about it a lot and it's probably easy sometimes to say we've changed our mindset and believe in ourselves.

"It feels different. Everybody has come in with a voice and a belief and are challenging each other to get better. Ultimately that's what grows a group quickly."

Wales believed they could create history - Lake

All Blacks ran into a Welsh brick wall - Barrett

Tandy believes Wales' young players need to be given the environment to express themselves.

"There's a young group that needed care," Tandy said.

"Those connection pieces we speak about a lot and it's something we pride ourselves on."

He highlighted players like Eddie James, Dan Edwards and Sam Costelow, among those gaining caps and growing in confidence.

"It's trying to give them the freedom to play, because it's a tough place to play in Wales when things are not going right," the Wales head coach added.

"They're young men and we want these players to go out there and play with freedom.

"They need to have that and we believe in that support for them, because sometimes it may be a little bit of a burden.

"We've got to make sure these boys have a safe space."

#2630. Dylan Harper plays the hero as Spurs beat Jazz, extend win streak to 12

It was an ugly one and too close for comfort, but the Spurs got their 12th win in a row in their visit to Salt Lake City. Despite not playing particularly well, San Antonio escaped with a 110-102 victory to hand the Jazz their 12th straight loss, in large part thanks to Dylan Harper fourth-quarter heroics.

All the ingredients required for a strange game that could get more complicated than expected for the Spurs were there. It was a Sunday matinee; De'Aaron Fox was out; the Jazz had already played the Silver and Black twice in the young season; it was a one-game road trip at altitude. Yet it was hard to imagine just how weird things would be, especially in the first half. Mo Bamba turning into Stephen Curry was hard to predict, and so was Jordan McLaughlin being the first guy to reach double digits for the visitors. San Antonio's defense being lethargic early was no surprise but the way Utah was making them pay by hitting jumpers was. On the other end, meanwhile, Fox was missed in the halfcourt, so transition offense had to pick up the slack. It wasn't the most well-played bout of the season, but it was entertaining and close, as the score was tied after one.

The Spurs have been relying on their talent to overwhelm opponents even when the execution and occasionally the energy have been far from ideal, and to some degree, they achieved that against the Jazz in the first half. This time, however, getting a superstar performance from Wembanyama and a couple of other contributors to step up simply wasn't enough to create a lead, like it has in past games. Utah was confident after the strong start and didn't let a few missed jumpers discourage them. Defensively, they had no answers for The Alien, who had his three-point shot going, but were happy to sit back and watch others fall into bad habits and take the bait of driving or shooting when the other option would have been preferable. It was clear that San Antonio was going to have to take the win, because the Jazz were not going to give it away without a fight.

During two different stretches of the third, it seemed like the Spurs were finally going to impose their will. A strong start allowed them to carve a double-digit lead, but errant shooting and lackadaisical defense followed, and the home team quickly caught up. Then when the bench checked in, they managed to put together a rare run for a group that has struggled often, putting the Silver and Black up nine after an alley-oop dunk from the oft-maligned Luke Kornet. Alas, Utah once again rallied after a timeout, shooting their way back while San Antonio's jumpers refused to fall. Holding serve while the second unit was in would have normally been enough if the starters had come in rested to close the frame strong, but it just didn't happen. The game was tied going into a final period, and it didn't feel impossible to see two streaks being snapped on a shocker of an ending.

Fortunately, an overall strange game finished with the most logical result. The Jazz, who have struggled with maintaining leads, especially at the end of games, looked like the young, shorthanded team that they are in the clutch. Keldon Johnson, last year's Sixth Man of the Year, was the sparkplug San Antonio needed all game long, but elevated his impact with some crucial plays late. And Dylan Harper, who showed in the playoffs that he's not scared of the big moments, took over as the first option that Wembanyama couldn't be because of how much attention Utah was paying to his every move on offense. The young guard dropped 18 of his career-high 31 in the final period to keep the Spurs close enough to take advantage of the mistakes the home team would make down the stretch. It wasn't the prettiest of wins, but it was enough to keep the streak going.

What makes Dylan Harper such a scary young player is that a lot of what he does at this point in his career, on both ends, seems mostly done on instinct and sheer talent. He's a smart, polished player in some ways, but in others, he just… does things that happen to get good results more often than not. For most of the game he wasn't particularly efficient and at times forced things, but when the team actually needed someone to take over, that same hyper-aggressiveness and confidence that sometimes leads to poor decisions was the reason why he was ready to explode offensively. Harper is already a fantastic player who will only get better as a decision-maker, which should terrify every other team in the league.

While Harper's heroics will rightfully get most of the attention, Wembanyama's first half was also needed for the Spurs to escape with a win. Moreover, the Jazz' devoting so much attention to him on dives to the basket opened things up for others, including Harper on his consecutive fourth-quarter threes. The big guy did his job.

The third spot on the podium belongs to Keldon Johnson. In a game in which Devin Vassell and Julian Champagnie combined for 10 points on 17 shots and Harrison Barnes and Carter Bryant didn't move the needle off the bench, San Antonio needed someone who wasn't a guard or a center to step up. Johnson's made contributions in different areas, as accurately reflected by his stat line. A great mix of aggressiveness on offense and energy plays for a veteran who continues to reinvent himself.

The Spurs missed Fox, which isn't surprising, since he's their best half-court orchestrator, but Stephon Castle slotted in nicely in his old role as primary playmaker and had 20 points and nine assists. Jordan McLaughlin was decent off the bench as well, hitting some shots in the first half. Against better opponents, Fox's absence could be a bigger problem, but San Antonio survived without him.

The Spurs will kick off a three-game homestand by taking on one of the best teams in the East. It should be a good test for a San Antonio team that has not faced a lot of good opponents lately.

#2629. Steelers suffer blowout loss to Bengals, fall to 6-3

In what was a game that displayed a severe gap between playoff hopefuls and true Super Bowl contenders, the Cincinnati Bengals defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers 38-18. At 7-2, the Bengals now have possession of first place in the AFC North, while Pittsburgh falls to 6-3.

The Bengals started the game with the ball, marching 80 yards in nine plays before three straight incompletions forced them to settle for a field goal. The Steelers answered with a three-and-out, and the Bengals then put together a second consecutive 13-play drive that resulted in a Joe Burrow touchdown pass to Drew Sample, one of four on the night for Burrow. The Steelers then went three-and-out again, and were given a gift in the form of an Evan McPherson missed field goal to keep the game at 10-0, but the offense did nothing with the chance to remain in the game, going 11 yards in five plays before punting. The Bengals then stepped on the throat of Pittsburgh, as Burrow found Chase Brown for a two-yard score to put Cincinnati up 17-0. The Steelers then put together their first real drive of the game, driving 42 yards in 10 plays to set up a Chris Boswell field goal to cut the lead to 17-3. However, the 1:25 left on the clock was more than enough for the Bengals. Burrow led a 57-yard drive that saw Dohnte Meyers catch Burrow's third touchdown pass of the night to go up 24-3 at the half.

In the third quarter, the Steelers lost four yards on seven plays to open the second half before punting. The Bengals answered with a Joe Burrow touchdown pass to Chase Brown, his second on the night, to go up 31-3. Pittsburgh would finally put a touchdown on the board with Aaron Rodgers finding DK Metcalf for a 22-yard score. Metcalf also caught the two-point conversion to make it a 31-11 game. The Bengals erased that score in just over two minutes, driving 49 yards in four plays before Samaje Perine scored to make it 38-11. A Pat Freiermuth touchdown ended the scoring, giving Cincinnati a 38-18 win.

There were plenty of noteworthy numbers that best describe just how outmatched the Steelers were. At one point in the game, the Bengals had 356 net passing yards to the Steelers' 4. Of the game's first 28 plays, 25 of them were run by the Bengals' offense. Ja'Marr Chase had more receiving yards (231) than the Steelers had total yards (221). The Steelers averaged just 3.8 yards per play, a number that saw a bump in garbage time, compared to the Bengals' 7.4.

Pittsburgh will now take their 6-3 record to Philadelphia in Week 11, a place they haven't won in 61 years.

#2626. Sharks beat Predators 4-2 to end Nashville's 7-game win streak

SAN JOSE, Calif. (AP) — Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith each had a goal and two assists as the San Jose Sharks snapped the Nashville Predators' seven-game win streak, 4-2 on Sunday night.

Ivar Stenberg had a goal and an assist and Collin Graf also scored for the Sharks, while Alex Nedeljkovic made 32 saves.

Nils Hoglander and Steven Stamkos scored for the Predators and Juuse Saros stopped 20 shots.

Smith opened the scoring with 7:35 left in the first period with his eighth goal of the season after a breakaway that left him all alone after Stenberg found him.

Graf made it 2-0 with 3:50 left in the first period with his third goal of the season and first in 11 games.

Stenberg made it 3-0 at 4:45 of the second period with his third goal of the season, as Smith found him right in front for a tap-in while Saros had lost his stick.

Nashville got on the board late in the second period when Hoglander scored his fifth of the season after San Jose wasn't able to clear the puck. Adam Wilsby had the assist.

Celebrini made it 4-1 at 7:40 of the third period, with assists from Smith and defenseman Jacob Trouba.

Nashville cut the lead to 4-2 with 3:25 left to play on a power-play goal by Stamkos, his 12th of the season. The puck just sneaked inside the post and the goal was upheld after a review.

The Sharks have yet to record a shutout this season.

Predators: Visit the Minnesota Wild on Tuesday night.

Sharks: Host the Calgary Flames on Tuesday night.

#2625. Recap: Rockets rout Wizards, 147-119

The Washington Wizards fell to the Houston Rockets, 147-119, on Sunday night at Capital One Arena, extending their losing streak to seven games. The Wizards trailed by as many as 37 points and were it-rebounded by 19.

Coming off a 30-point performance against the Detroit Pistons on Thursday, Alex Sarr scored eight quick points on 3-of-3 shooting, including a three-pointer, to give Washington an early 13-12 lead.

The Wizards closed the first quarter trailing 36-31, with Sarr leading the way with 10 points. Anthony Davis, who also scored 30 against Detroit on Thursday, had a much quieter start, missing all three of his field-goal attempts, including several looks around the rim.

Houston opened the second quarter with a 7-0 run and eventually stretched its lead to 12. Sarr briefly halted the momentum with another three-pointer, but the Rockets continued to pull away. Houston's lead reached 17 with 6:29 remaining in the half, as Amen Thompson and Kevin Durant helped fuel the offensive surge. Thompson started 3-for-3 from beyond the arc, while Houston shot 56% from three-point range in the first half.

Washington went into the break trailing 73-54 despite Sarr's 15 points, four rebounds and two assists. The rest of the Wizards' starting lineup — Trae Young, AJ Dybantsa, Kyshawn George and Davis — combined for just 18 points.

Houston picked up right where it left off to start the third quarter, opening the period with a 12-4 run, and the game wasn't competitive from that point forward.

Thompson (26 points), Durant (25), Tari Eason (25) and Alperen Sengun (21) all scored 20+, while Sarr (25) was the only Wizard to finish with more than 20 points. Dybantsa scored 16 and grabbed seven boards, Davis finished with 14 points and eight rebounds, and George tacked on 11 points and four assists. Will Riley knocked down two three pointers and scored 14 points off the bench.

The Wizards will turn around to host the Memphis Grizzlies on Monday night at 7:00 p.m. ET at Capital One Arena.

#2624. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2623. The Bengals and Steelers final score has never happened before in NFL history

Earlier on Sunday, the Dallas Cowboys and San Fransisco 49ers played a game that ended with the 1099th unique score in NFL history. On Sunday night, the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers finished with the 1100th unique score in NFL history.

It's the second time this season we've had two Scorigamis in one weekend.

It is the second Bengals Scorigami of the year following their 43-36 win two weeks ago.

When we get a new final score in the NFL, it's called Scorigami. Normally when we get a Scorigami it's because a team scores an absolute boatload of points and often something weird happens, usually with two-point conversions. We got both on Sunday with the Bengals and Steelers.

The Bengals just kept scoring, taking a 31-3 game early in the fourth quarter. It's a pretty typical 28-point, four-touchdown lead. Nothing weird. Then the Pittsburgh Steelers scored a touchdown and went for two. If turned a three-touchdown deficit into a… three-touchdown deficit. Really not sure when the Steelers chose to do it. That 31-11 score would have been a Scorigami.

The Bengals scored again very quickly and kicked an extra point to make it 38-11. That would not have been Scorigami but the Steelers scored one last time and kicked the extra point to make it 38-18 for the Scorigami.

The only 38-point winners that haven't hit now are 38-2 and 38-4.

Our friends at Secret Base have done extensive work on Scorigami. If you want to see it, it is fascinating.

This is the fifth Scorigami of the 2026 NFL season.

September 13: Chicago Bears 59, Carolina Panthers 37

September 13: Minnesota Vikings 39, Green Bay Packers 22

November 1: Cincinnati Bengals 43, Tennessee Titans 36

November 15: San Francisco 49ers 46, Dallas Cowboys 40

November 15: Cincinnati Bengals 38, Pittsburgh Steelers 18

#2620. Raptors fall to defending champs in overtime

The Toronto Raptors hosted the New York Knicks in the first of a home-and-home series tonight, a hard-fought, at times frustrating, and eventual narrow loss to the tune of 108-112. While this is their fourth straight loss, the seventh to a team over with.a better record, and another game where they gave up a double-digit lead, this wasn't a complete loss. Instead, it was an opportunity to see just how well the Raptors can play, making the defending champions sweat a little.

Scottie Barnes had a great first game back, barely missing a step as he found his shot from all over the floor, leading the team with 30 points, 9 boards, and 4 assists. Jamal Shead was undoubtedly Toronto's biggest difference maker though, with his intensity, speed, and facilitation shifting the tone of the game entirely in Toronto's favour every time he touched the floor. He contributed 19 points, 2 rebounds, and 4 assists. RJ, IQ, and Poeltl all chipped in double digit points as well.

Jalen Brunson played phenomenally for the Knicks, finishing with 28 points and 9 assists. OG Anunoby and Karl Anthony Towns contributed to the game as well to the tune of 21 points and 9 rebounds and 28 points and 17 rebounds, respectively. Landrey Shamet proved to be a solid bench option for New York, connecting well from long range and scoring 23 points including four 3s.

New York is still trying to find their way this year despite carrying over much of their championship roster from last year. Coach Mike Brown doesn't seem fazed in the slightest though, saying he's "happy where we are right now", recognizing the recent growing pains will better prepare them for the future. If they identify and deal with these problems now, they won't crop up as the playoffs. Especially important when you're defending a title.

Of course, for Knicks fans, some of the issues feel worth worrying about. The trifecta of their biggest concerns were things Toronto, at times, tried to capitalize on. Going into this game, New York is the slowest team in the League based on pace, with a far worse transition game than last year. Being able to get back and set up defensively is a huge asset to limit easy possessions, which actually leads to the Knicks' second problem. They are one of the worst shooting teams in the league right now, forcing contested shots in the paint rather than regrouping and making smart plays. This leads them to being the third-most blocked team in the NBA currently. Protecting the paint is crucial, Scottie and CMB the most capable of doing so. Finally, despite having some great individual defenders, collectively as a team they've underperformed, ranking 22nd and 27th in steals and blocks respectively. Taking advantage of their lacklustre defence through ball movement and finding the best shot should make the offence easy.

Scottie "our best player" Barnes was back in the lineup, a welcome sight for everyone. He took absolutely no time announcing his present, rolling off a screen and soaring in to dunk over defenders in the first possession of the game. He had 10 of their first 13 points, making a pair of long range shots in the process. An excellent indicator to his readiness to be back.

Collin Murray-Boyles got the start ahead of Poeltl, in an effort to match up better against Karl Anthony Towns who plays more as a stretch than a traditional centre. He did well, as KAT's early scoring was the result of switches that freed him from CMB.

Toronto certainly capitalized on those weaknesses early, allowing them to stay in the game despite their own turnovers, defensive lapses, and shooting struggles throughout the first quarter. They ended the frame 7-22 from the floor, but remained only two possessions behind the Knicks, 17-23.

Despite a low-scoring first quarter, there was no shortage of bodies flying to secure extra possessions when the ball was loose. Unsurprisingly, this started to translate into chippiness. Scottie Barnes almost dropped Tyler Kolek by ripping the ball from his hands. Alijah Martin thrived in this atmosphere, and was able to draw a flagrant foul from Jordan Clarkson likely from his peskiness.

The Knicks started to take their game outside the three-point line, finding a lot more success than inside the paint. New York gradually started to build a lead, but Toronto countered well, working to run them off the line and forced them to make unfavourable shots. At the same time, their own shots were starting to fall, allowing them to work their way back and eventually tie the game. Jamal Shead made his presence known with a pair of fast-break full-speed layups.

The Raptors continued to probe the paint and found more success than from beyond the arc but New York fought harder in the final minutes of the half, heading to the locker room with a narrow 47-43 lead.

The third quarter wasn't smooth sailing by any means. Unforced turnovers and miscommunications on the offensive cost the Raptors possessions. Toronto's defense kept them in the game through these slumps, forcing the Knicks to take tough shots that weren't falling for them. CMB was in foul trouble before the halfway point of the third quarter, forcing him to head to the bench, but in his absence, Poeltl managed to play solid defence in the middle.

The biggest shift came with the presence of Shead on the floor. He continued to push the pace in his minutes, forcing New York on their heels. Without a set defence, Shead was able to dictate the game, distributing to the open man but also making his own shots. In a departure to his last few games, where he was left open on the 3-point line, struggling to make shots, he feasted from long range, cashing in back-to-back buckets and forcing the Knicks to respect him. This energy gave Toronto their first significant advantage since the first frame, closing the third with a 74-67 lead.

Toronto showed flashes of disorganization again in the final frame, still working on their ability to finish games. New York weren't willing to yield and the Raptors weren't trying hard enough on every possession. Give-away rebounds that allowed the Knicks to get second and third chances were their undoing to an extent, leaving the door open for New York to get back into a game that they previously trailed by double-digits. A series of empty trips seemingly sucked all of the air out of the building until Scottie Barnes took over. The Raptors lead was back, going shot for shot with the Knicks in the final seconds, cashing in a game-tying three-pointer. Then he put his body on the line, tossing himself on the floor to trap the ball and prevent the Knicks from getting a final shot up, forcing OT.

Extra time matched the tone of the first 48 minutes of the game, with fans on their feet from start to finish. Scottie led offensively, CMB had a phenomenal block that sent the ball deep into the stands, and they were all tied up.

Inhuman shot-making by Brunson meant that the Raptors were once again behind. Clutch free-throws from Walter allowed Toronto to try and foul to regain possession, but they weren't able to make the final shot, submitting to the Knicks in overtime.

After the game, Darko attributed the loss to poor decision-making at points throughout the game, and especially in the final minutes. Shead echoed this, pointing to missed rebounds and lapses in judgement, saying "we played 44 minutes of good basketball", remarking that this is a growing experience for them, and all it will do is make them better.

They'll have their chance to make up for tonight's loss and finally break their losing streak versus the Knicks on Tuesday when they host them for a second time. Tune in at 7:30pm ET on Sportsnet.

#2618. Knicks 112, Raptors 108 (OT): Scenes from our first bonus basketball of the season

There's trouble when Mike Breen calls the Knicks out. Right before tip-off, the lifelong fan and broadcasting GOAT called them a "mediocre" basketball team, then acknowledged that they know it's a problem and they're trying to fix it. We noticed it, too; New York had lost two straight and been outhustled by the outclassed Indiana Pacers on Friday.

For 40 minutes tonight, the Knicks proved Mike's case. They led after one because Toronto couldn't shoot, and much the same was true at halftime. Then the Dinos began to pull away, nearly doubling up the Knicks in the paint and beating them to the boards. The Americans trailed by seven to start the fourth and by as many as 14 before finally showing some fire and desire. They went ahead with less than a minute left, but Scottie Barnes (30 PTS, 9 RBS, -9) scored Toronto's last nine points to force overtime. The Knicks never trailed in the fifth frame, and a Brunson dagger with 33 seconds left put them ahead for good, 112-108.

Back from a groin injury, Barnes scored 10 of Toronto's first 13 points, hitting back-to-back threes to put the Raptors up 13-4. Scottie was merriment and light while the Knicks were a smear of discouragement. Birthday boy Karl-Anthony Towns (28 PTS, 17 RBS) pitched two passes into the front row in the first four minutes, and Jalen Brunson (28 PTS, 9 AST, 41 MIN) had three dimes and one basket in the quarter. The bench improved matters. A Mikal Bridges (5 PTS, 7 RBS, 32 MIN . . . +15!) steal and a Towns bunny sparked a 9-0 run that included five points from Landry Shamet (23 PTS, 30 MIN, +12) and a tying dunk from Andre Drummond, courtesy of Josh Hart (0 PTS, 5 RBS, 26 MIN, -15).

Allen Graves stripped Brunson and Jakob Poeltl laid it in at the other end to put Toronto up 17-14. Then the Dinos, hardly renowned for their shooting, came up blank for the final 3:45. Tyler Kolek fed Towns for the tying three and Miles McBride for the one that made it 23-17 at the break.

Shamet scored six quick points to put the Knicks up 32-22. He hit a three after Kolek picked off an RJ Barrett pass, then made all three free throws after Barrett fouled him on another attempt. Toronto answered with a 14-2 run. Poeltl picked Jordan Clarkson's pocket and finished at the other end, starting center Collin Murray-Boyles dunked back a shot Shamet had blocked, and Jamal Shead (19 PTS) scored eight points in 76 seconds to put the Raptors ahead 38-36. During Toronto's 10-0 stretch, the Knicks burned a full shot clock and missed four straight shots.

OG Anunoby stopped the run with two free throws, and Towns put New York back in front with a three. Barrett tied it at 42, but Brunson answered with a step-back three, his only field goal of the quarter. Bridges, who'd barely figured into the offense, set up that shot with 45 seconds left and hit his first basket, a 21-footer, with seven seconds to go. Barnes managed just two points in the second, and Barrett had as many turnovers as baskets (two).

The Knicks were lucky to lead 47-43 at the half. The shooting gap was small (44% to 41%), but Toronto owned the paint, 26-14, won the boards by four, and turned 12 Knicks giveaways into 16 points. The three-ball kept our heroes afloat (42% to Toronto's 26%). For those keeping track, Bridges was 1-for-2 for two points, with two rebounds, an assist, and a steal . . . but stay tuned for this:

On to Q3: the Knicks led 57-54 midway through the third before Toronto scored seven straight. Brunson's three cut it to 63-62, but the Raptors answered with an 11-0 run, including two Shead threes (the kid was cooking). Barrett had eight points and three assists, and Shead scored nine as Toronto won the quarter 31-20 and took a 74-67 lead into the fourth. Cap scored 13 of New York's 20 points, KAT had four, Bridges made one free throw, and Hart continued to deal with a devastating allergy to buckets.

On to Q4: Immanuel Quickley hit two threes from at least 29 feet to put Toronto up 84-71 with 8:55 left. The Knicks answered with a 12-2 run. Kolek found Anunoby for two quick buckets, and Towns picked Barrett's pocket to send Bridges the other way for a layup. Towns had 15 points and seven rebounds in the quarter, while Brunson went scoreless but handed out five assists.

Down five with under two minutes left, New York scored seven straight. Bridges grabbed the offensive board that set up Shamet's tying three, and Towns put the Knicks ahead with a hook. Towns then hit from 28 feet to make it 95-92 with 20 seconds left, but Barnes answered with a step-back three six seconds later. He had 11 in the quarter and put the clamps on Brunson as time expired.

On to OT: Shamet and Brunson scored seven apiece in the bonus frame. Quickley kept Toronto close with two early buckets, one off a Bridges turnover. Barnes whiffed on free throws with 1:47 left, banked in a three to tie it at 104, and lobbed to Murray-Boyles to tie it again at 106. Out of a timeout, Bridges found Brunson for the go-ahead fadeaway three with 33 seconds left. Anunoby hit both free throws to restore the three-point cushion, Barnes missed a chance to tie it, Towns grabbed his 17th rebound, and then he split a pair at the line to seal the win.

Mo is gassing up his recap. The Knicks stay over the border for game with the Raps on Tuesday. Rest up, Knickerbockers.

#2617. 2027 NFL Draft Order: Winless Chargers hold No. 1 spot as Titans, Dolphins loom in Week 10

It's never too early to start looking ahead to the 2027 NFL Draft, right?

Week 10 of the current NFL season isn't even close over yet, but the order for the draft in a few months is already starting to take shape. And, at least for now, the Los Angeles Chargers are still very much in control of the No. 1 overall pick.

The Chargers will enter their Monday Night Football matchup with the Baltimore Ravens as the league's only winless team. They sit at just 0-8 on the year.

But if the Chargers win on Monday night in Baltimore, they'll join both the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins with 1-8 records. The Titans fell to the Jacksonville Jaguars in a 40-23 blowout on Sunday afternoon, which marked their third straight loss and moved them to 0-5 at Nissan Stadium this season. The Dolphins just barely lost to the Indianapolis Colts 24-22 on Sunday. The win snapped the Colts' five-game losing skid, yet it only moved them to 3-7 on the year. The Dolphins have now lost three straight heading into a road game against the Buffalo Bills next week.

While they have the same record, the Titans currently have the edge over the Dolphins for the No. 2 overall pick. The New York Jets and Philadelphia Eagles then round out the top five.

Now even though things are undoubtedly bad, the Chargers will realistically win at least one game the rest of the way. The NFL hasn't seen a team go a full season without winning a game since the 2017 Cleveland Browns. That means that either the Titans or Dolphins can sneak in and steal the No. 1 overall draft pick from the Chargers down the stretch. The Jets and Eagles, both with just two wins this season, aren't out of the question yet, either.

For now, though, the Chargers are in control of that top spot.

#2614. NHL Power Rankings: Flyers flounder to start new season as Rick Tocchet searches for answers

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

I hate to get so negative just one week into the season, but the Philadelphia Flyers have forced my hand. After a magical run to the second round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Flyers have fallen on their face through four games.

Philadelphia opened the season with a 7-0 loss to the rival Pittsburgh Penguins, and coach Rick Tocchet described his team's play as "disturbing." There was only one way for the season to go after that, right? Wrong.

The Flyers are off to an 0-2-2 start, and the underlying numbers aren't pretty. Per Natural Stat Trick, they have a five-on-five expected goals share of 26.0%, which ranks last in the NHL. Their 4.57 xGA/60 also ranks last. Their 1.94 xGF/60? You guessed it. Last.

Tocchet's bunch entered the season with a lot of well-earned optimism. Even with subpar play from Matvei Michkov last season, the Flyers managed to reach the Eastern Conference Semifinals. Rookie Porter Martone asserted himself as a budding star with six goals and nine assists in 19 games between the regular season and playoffs.

There's still plenty of time -- 80 games exactly -- for the Flyers to get back on track and restore that optimism, but to say this has been a discouraging start would be an understatement.

#2610. Germany player ratings vs. Serbia: Gruda steals the show on dream debut

Germany won their crucial encounter in the Nations League against Serbia with 3-1.

Below are our player ratings for Jürgen Klopp's side on a scale from 1 to 10, with 10 being the highest possible score.

Produced two important saves to keep Germany's comfortable lead - otherwise the game could've shifted. Held onto anything else that was directed his way and distribution was borderline flawless.

All in all, a solid night at right-back for the Freiburg man who did the basics well. Perhaps could have done more going forward, but he covered for Gruda and gave him the freedom to be creative.

Solid performance, but nothing that stood out. Seemed somewhat slow in two counter-attacking instances.

The Newcastle United man won the vast majority of his duels and maintained a strong pass completion rate. A great partner to Tah in this match.

A couple of decent moments going forward and linked up well with Derry Scherhant on the left flank. Definitely went into the match with much confidence from his stellar performances for Stuttgart. At the moment, the preferred option over Nathaniel Brown and David Raum.

CDM: Aleksandar Pavlović – 8/10 (until 74')

Another great game from the man with Serbian roots. First Germany start as a CDM next to Bayern partner Kimmich. The duo worked well - but was that really a surprise? Great pre-assist for Germany's second goal.

Led his team into the rain battle of Belgrade with much confidence. Even scored a nice long shot, but it wasn't given due to an offside postion from teammate Havertz.

Another debutant under Klopp - and what a debut it was. Gruda proved why he deserved this start over Bayern star Lennart Karl. Really good in 1v1 duels, amazing solo goal just after halftime. A promising start to his National team career.

Managed to orchestrate a lot of neat give-and-go moves around the edge of the box to set up teammates. Didn't really get into shooting positions himself, apart from his rebound-goal.

Really lively on the ball - but that was rare in comparison with his teammates. Made no mistakes, but almost seemed hidden throughout the game. Had a great moment to almost score in the 70th. Solid game.

Havertz continues to be the main man for Germany up-front. Doesn't need many chances, but always seems to be involved in goals in the end. Deciding header to get Germany in front after just two minutes. BUT, he should have scored the second (just before Wirtz cleaned up for him).

What a way to announce yourself on the international stage! Brajan Gruda showed exactly why he deserved a place in the starting XI ahead of Bayern youngster Lennart Karl. The Leipzig winger was a constant threat, looked sharp in one-on-one situations and capped an impressive performance with a brilliant solo goal shortly after half-time. Unplayable at times. His confidence, directness and ability to take on defenders made him one of Germany's standout performers throughout the evening. A dream start to his international career and a Man of the Match-worthy display against Serbia.

Tampa Bay attempts to complete a sweep of the 2026 ALDS when they square off against New York at 8 p.m. ET in Game 3 on Wednesday at Yankee Stadium. The Rays, who defeated the Yankees in this round in 2020 en route to the second World Series appearance in franchise history, edged New York 1-0 in this year's series opener before pushing their AL East rivals to the brink of elimination with a 5-2 victory in Game 2.

The Rays went 7-6 against New York during the regular season but lost four of the six contests at Yankee Stadium, including three of four in their penultimate series of the campaign. Tampa Bay was outscored 15-6 in its final two games in the Bronx, but its pitching staff has kept the Yankees in check thus far in the ALDS.

New York was limited to one hit in Game 1 as Drew Rasmussen had a no-hitter for 7 2/3 innings before Austin Wells ripped a double down the right field line. However, Wells made an ill-advised decision to try and stretch it into a triple and was thrown out easily at third base. Rays closer Bryan Baker worked a perfect ninth to preserve the win.

The Yankees didn't fare much better offensively in Game 2 as they registered just four hits, two of which were solo homers by Ben Rice. They were even worse defensively, committing four errors -- including three in the first inning that helped give Tampa Bay a 1-0 lead.

Tampa Bay will look to punch its ticket to the ALCS behind Nick Martinez, who set a career high with 15 wins this year and matched another with a 3.10 ERA. The 36-year-old right-hander posted a better ERA on the road (2.38) than at home (3.90) during the regular season and had a 2.16 mark in two turns at Yankee Stadium.
