#2608. SCORIGAMI: The NFL’s list of unique scores has added more in 2026

There had been 1095 unique final scores in NFL history as of the conclusion of the 2025 season. We are now up to 1099 with the ones added during 2026.

With teams scoring more points in games, the extra point moving out to a 33-yard kick, and teams deciding to go for two more often to gain edges, never-before-seen final scores are still happening despite the NFL playing for more than 100 years. These unique scores are also called "Scorigami".

Many of the Scorigami we are seeing are for 40-plus point games that have high scoring from both teams, but we've also been seeing scores in the 30s that have never happened. It's not just high scores that have never happened, though. A game has never finished in a 2-2 tie, for instance. The NFL didn't allow two-point conversions until 1994, and we've never seen an 8-7 game. A game has never ended in a 9-9 tie, among other scores still out there.

Since 1992, there have been three or more Scoigamis in every season. The average since the start of the 2000 season is seven per year with the high of 14 in 2013 and a low of three in 2022 and 2009.

The 2026 NFL season didn't wait to get the Scorigami train rolling. Two NFC North teams won games on the Sunday of opening weekend with scores that had never happened before. They were the 1096th and 1097th unique scores in NFL history.

Normally when we get a Scorigami, it's because something weird happened in the game. This one wasn't that. The Bears just laid the smack down. Chicago scored 14 points in the first, third, and fourth quarters along with a 17-point third quarter. All of those are regular scores, there were just a lot of them. We had a late extra point blocked, but 59-38 also has never happened.

The Packers missed an extra point in the first quarter, but that didn't trigger a whole lot of unique scores on its own. Everything stayed pretty normal until the fourth quarter when Minnesota scored to take the lead. They converted a 2-point conversion to go up 25-22. Scoring 25 points in an NFL game is weird. Then Minnesota added two more 7-point touchdowns on top of it. A 39-point day is pretty rare. (A 32-22 score has also never happened.)

After a two-point conversion made the score a very normal 21-21, things got weird. A Bengals safety made it 23-21. The Bengals couldn't get a two-point conversion on a later touchdown after the Titans scored, making it 29-28. Then the Titans got a two-point on their next score to make it a seven-point lead at 36-29. The Bengals scored and kicked an extra point and the game sat at 36-36 at the end of regulation. It should be noted that an overtime touchdown would have won the game without an extra point before this season and 42-36 has happened before.

The Cowboys didn't get the extra point after scoring a touchdown, which made it 16-10 in the second quarter. In the fourth quarter, the score was 38-19 when the Cowboys got in the end zone and tried to make it an 11-point game but failed at 38-25. That's when things got weirder. Dallas made it 38-32 then the 49ers scored a long touchdown with a 2-point conversion to get the to the very strange 46 points. 46-32 was a Scorigami, as was 46-39, but the Cowboys went for 2 after their last TD and got it to 46-40. Also a Scorigami.

For the second time on the same day, we saw a Scorrigami. And it was the Bengals' second in three weeks. With the Bengals up 31-2, the Steelers scored and went for two to make it 31-11. it's weird because it's still a three-touchdown game and doesn't really help him close the gap but whatever. While 31-11 would have been Scorigami, both teams scored again to make it 38-18. The only 38-point Scorigami winners left now are 38-2 and 38-4.

8-7: Someone scores a late touchdown and goes for the win, not the tie

9-9: Two struggling offenses end in a 9-9 tie, or a 6-6 game at end of regulation ending this way

25-18: A few ways to get to 18 then a score to win

32-22: A team playing catch up gets to 22 and a team keeping them away gets to 32

41-41: With 40-40 off the board, lets go one more

42-25: A team up late pushes it to a three-possession game

46-17: It's the lowest number against the very common 17

50-3: It's the lowest number against the very common 3

60-14: It's the lowest number against the very common 14

After seven Scorigamis in 2024, there were four NFL games to hit new finals in 2025, two including the high-scoring Buffalo Bills. here is how each of them got there in chronological order:

This game features two high-powered offenses at the height of their powers, but the Bills started going for two in the third quarter and missed on consecutive attempts. Halfway through the fourth quarter, they sat at 25 points, a rare number. A missed extra point by the Ravens put Baltimore at 40 — not an entirely uncommon number on its own — before the Bills' final push. Buffalo made it 40-38 after two touchdowns and an extra point but failed to convert on the game-tying two-point conversion. They got the ball back and kicked a field goal as time expired to win 41-40.

There are several ties still available on this list, but not as many as you would think. The NFL didn't have sudden death overtime until 1974 when they added a 15-minute frame, so there were a bunch of ties prior to 1974 but then a lot fewer. They modified the rule in 2010 so it wasn't sudden death for a first-drive field goal then shortened the time to 10 minutes in 2017. In 2025, they gave every team a possession. With those recent changes, ties can be more common.

Those rule changes directly impacted this game between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers. Dallas didn't win after their first-possession field goal because Green Bay was guaranteed a possession. The Packers only had 4:40 on the clock and drove deep into Dallas territory. After shots to the end zone failed, they settled for a 40-40 tie as time expired.

In the third quarter, the Jaguars were up 23-10 and scored another touchdown. Up 19, they knew the Texans had to score three times to win so they tried to make it a 21-point lead to make it three touchdowns to tie or win. That play failed, and they sat at 29 points with a 19-point lead.

The Texans then scored a touchdown plus a two-point conversion to make it an 11-point game. Another touchdown with a failed two-point conversion made it a 5-point game. Houston scored again to go up 30-29 and tried another two-point conversion to ensure a late field goal wouldn't beat them, but that try failed with 31 seconds on the clock.

Here's where things get nuts. A 30-29 score has happened before. But the Texans returned a fumble for a touchdown to make it 36-29 as time expired. A final of 37-29 and 38-29 has happened, but because there was no time on the clock, there was no extra point attempt, and the final stood at Scorigami.

For Buffalo's second Scorigami of the year, they also topped 40 points. The Buccaneers started the shenanigans in the third quarter when they scored a touchdown to make it 26-21. They went for two to try and make it 28-21 but the conversion failed. Buffalo got to 31 the old-fashioned way, with four touchdowns and PATs plus a field goal, and the score was 31-26. After another touchdown, the Bucs tried to make it a three-point lead with another two-point conversion that failed, sticking them at 32 points. Buffalo scored another touchdown to make it 37-32 and failed the two-point conversion to try and make it a seven-point game. The Bills' final touchdown game them a 43-32 lead and Buffalo pushed it to 44-32 with an extra point to make it a two-touchdown lead with 2:35 left.

#2606. Mahomes throws five touchdowns as Chiefs thrash Falcons

Patrick Mahomes proved he is back to his imperious best with five touchdowns and 348 passing yards as the Kansas City Chiefs thrashed the Falcons 35-13 at Atlanta on Sunday.

In the three-time Super Bowl champion quarterback's most impressive showing since a nine-month injury absence with torn knee ligaments, Mahomes completed 22-of-35 passes with zero interceptions and one sack.

Victory took the Chiefs level with the idle Denver Broncos at the top of the AFC West, on 7-2.

Rookie Emmett Johnson twice found the end zone, while Josh Downs had a touchdown on his Kansas City debut following a deadline day trade from Indianapolis.

Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong each scored their first Chiefs touchdowns, grabbing passes of 39 yards and 43 yards respectively.

"It just showcases another level to our offense, that we can continue to get better and better," said Mahomes.

Johnson -- stepping up for Kenneth Walker III, who was absent with a groin injury -- also led the Chiefs' running game, with 22 carries for 101 yards.

"I thought we did a great job picking up, obviously Kenneth not being here. I thought Emmett did a great job," said Mahomes.

It was another miserable day for the Falcons, who trailed 28-3 before Bijan Robinson's fourth-quarter touchdown, and have lost five of their past six.

San Francisco beat the Dallas Cowboys 46-40 in a high-scoring, back-and-forth duel.

The 49ers had moved 19 points clear in the second half at Dallas, as Deebo Samuel scored a 70-yard touchdown from a trick play and Christian McCaffrey added another.

Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott rallied his team with two touchdowns, before McCaffrey took a Brock Purdy pass 66 yards to seemingly put the game to bed.

But CeeDee Lamb grabbed another touchdown in the final minute and Dallas converted the two-point attempt, to ensure a nervy finish.

Victory moved San Francisco to a joint NFL-best 8-1, along with Buffalo who beat the misfiring New York Jets 31-12.

Returning to the Minnesota Vikings on trade deadline day Tuesday, Kirk Cousins threw for two touchdowns to beat divisional rivals Green Bay 30-10.

Cousins spent six successful seasons with the Vikings but tore his Achilles tendon at the Packers' Lambeau Field in 2023, and subsequently left for stints at Atlanta and Las Vegas before returning this week.

"It was emotional, coming to the stadium three years ago, tearing my Achilles here... it's been a tough three years," said Cousins.

The Cleveland Browns rallied from 17-0 down to stun the Houston Texans 27-24, as Quinshon Judkins ran in a touchdown with less than a minute remaining.

Houston led with C.J. Stroud's first-half passing touchdowns to Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson, but allowed Cleveland two touchdowns and two field goals without reply.

The Texans thought they had salvaged the win with a Dalton Schultz touchdown, before Watson led yet another late game-winning drive with 53 seconds left.

"Personally for me it was definitely special," said Watson, who was drafted by Houston in 2017 and traded to Cleveland five years later.

The Detroit Lions thrashed New England 35-10 in Munich, Germany.

Patriots quarterback Drake Maye left the field with an ankle injury following a sack by Aidan Hutchinson -- who suffered a knee injury celebrating the sack.

Jahmyr Gibbs had 153 rushing yards with two touchdowns, and another 99 receiving yards, in the Lions' fifth straight win.

The Carolina Panthers needed a field goal with two seconds remaining to beat their divisional rival New Orleans Saints 20-17 and move top of the NFC South.

Indianapolis snapped their five-game losing streak with a 24-22 win over Miami.

Super Bowl champions Seattle beat Las Vegas 21-13, ensuring a frustrating debut start for Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The top draft pick was sacked six times, but opened the scoring with his first NFL touchdown.

In Sunday's final game, Cincinnati stormed to a fifth straight win, crushing Pittsburgh 38-18, with another four touchdowns and 409 yards for in-form Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow.

#2605. As LeBron soars up all-time assist list, his teammates need to have their hands ready

Fourteen games into the season, the Sixers are noticing the LeBron James effect in just about every facet of life. After a win over the Indiana Pacers, Tyrese Maxey zoomed to the podium to knock out his media availability with the majority of the Sixers beat in the locker room interviewing James.

"I love LeBron James," Maxey said as he sat down in front of a room with only a couple reporters.

Of course, they're noticing it in plenty of ways on the court as well. That win saw LeBron record 11 assists, good enough to move him up ahead of Jason Kidd for third in all-time career assists. He now only trails Chris Paul and John Stockton.

It may not sound like it would be, but playing next to such a prolific passer is something they have to get used to. The fact that your teammate could hit you with the ball at any given moment is an adjustment.

On the first play of the game, Maxey was cutting down the baseline just for the sake of cutting through. He thought all he was doing was helping create space on the side of the floor he was vacating, not realizing that LeBron had found him wide open under the basket.

"I was not planning to get the ball and the ball hit me in my chest and I looked up I was at the rim so I had to lay it in and I missed it," Maxey said, "but it's just like plays like that where you got to be ready at all times."

The idea of being ready for the ball at any time when James is on the floor is something that the Sixers are trying to make a point of emphasis. As was the case with Maxey's smoked bunny, the process of learning that can look ugly at times.

James joked that the key to guys figuring it out is to "hit 'em in the head a couple of times." According to James, VJ Edgecombe was a particularly frequent victim of that during training camp.

"Even when you don't think you're open, you're gonna be open," is what James told Edgecombe and, frankly, all of his teammates. "I just tell my guys, always be paying attention to me when I got the ball because I definitely see plays develop before they happen."

Off-ball movement is often looked at as "dirty work" in the NBA, something the Sixers haven't excelled at in recent years. Because of James' ability to reward cutters, it's made the Sixers not just buy into it, but happy to do so.

"He makes you want to cut. He makes you want to play without the ball," Maxey said. "He makes you want to always have your hands ready and be ready to score the ball because he's that unselfish and he's going to find you."

They say raw assist numbers are not the truest mark of a passer or a facilitator. One of James' best assists of the game against Indiana was not given to him in the stat sheet, but it was entirely created by what he saw from outside the perimeter.

Dean Wade cut out of the strong side corner to open that up from the ball handlers, before hearing James tell him to run back. James saw that Wade's defender would help on Edgecombe once Edgecombe drove to the basket, leaving Wade wide open for a corner three. Steve Jones, a brilliant Xs and Os guy for The Dunker Spot, clipped the play.

After being around James for training camp and a handful of regular season games, Wade said he's not really surprised by LeBron's ability to make that kind of read in the moment.

"He sees everything that's going on," Wade said. "He knows what their defense is doing."

James has had a reputation for being able to diagnose opposing team's plays as they're being called. Pacers head coach Rick Carlisle, who called James an "NBA basketball AI machine," said that LeBron is the reason he doesn't have play calls anymore. James said that ability is something he's just always had with him.

"I've always, since I was a kid, had the ability to see plays before they actually happened," he said, "seeing the movement, being able to see like cracks in the defense before they was even open. It's something that's been with me since I was a kid."

The Sixers have struggled so far to put together all of this absurd offensive talent in a way that really clicks. Even after beating the Pacers, they are still 19th in the league in points per 100 possessions, per Cleaning the Glass.

Getting used to the tendencies of one of the best passers of all time should help things look smoother as the season goes on.

#2604. Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

#2603. Steelers report card Week 10: Ugly grades for Aaron Rodgers, DK Metcalf in Bengals loss

The Pittsburgh Steelers were hammered by the Cincinnati Bengals, 38-18, in their "Sunday Night Football" matchup that decided control of the AFC North.

The Bengals now take a one-game lead heading into the second half of the season, with both teams facing fairly soft schedules.

First-year coach Mike McCarthy's squad will now have to play catch-up against their division rival that looked invincible at times, outgaining the Steelers by a 484-221 margin en route to the blowout victory.

Here's USA TODAY Sports' report card on the Steelers' performance.

Aaron Rodgers did not complete a pass until about 20 minutes into the game. By that point, Bengals counterpart Joe Burrow had already thrown for close to 250 yards and two touchdowns as his team took a 17-0 first-half lead. Rodgers' happy feet were noticeable. Some of that was due to significant pressure at times, but he never really seemed in sync, even when he had time to throw. And when he did, he was frequently inaccurate. He finished the night 15-of-29 passing for 143 yards. It was one of his worst performances as a Steeler before he padded the stats somewhat late.

Jaylen Warren did not make many people miss. You can blame some of that on poor run blocking in front of him. Warren has put himself among the NFL's leaders in scrimmage yards with a ton of yards after contact, however. When he's not getting those yards, it noticeably impacts this offense. His offensive line has to be better, but we can't let him completely off the hook here either.

The drops never seem to end for DK Metcalf. He had multiple in this one and registered zero catches in the first half, when the Steelers still had a chance to make it a game. The former Pro Bowler is supposed to be a safety blanket for Rodgers in games like this one. The guy Rodgers knows he can find with some level of consistency, even when other things aren't working offensively. He's definitively not that right now, in the second year of his five-year, $150 million contract, which was signed after he was acquired in a trade with the Seattle Seahawks in the 2025 offseason. The Steelers need Michael Pittman Jr. back as soon as possible, and Metcalf's garbage-time touchdown does little to change that reality.

Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin smiles after being interviewed by NBC broadcaster Dan Patrick after Super Bowl XLIII at Raymond James Stadium on Feb. 1, 2009. The Steelers defeated the Arizona Cardinals, 27-23, in one of the most exciting Super Bowls ever played.

Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin smiles after being interviewed by NBC broadcaster Dan Patrick after Super Bowl XLIII at Raymond James Stadium on Feb. 1, 2009. The Steelers defeated the Arizona Cardinals, 27-23, in one of the most exciting Super Bowls ever played.

Pat Freiermuth has had some of the best days of his career against the Bengals defense, but like Metcalf, he was almost invisible until the late fourth-quarter touchdown that didn't matter. He received just one first-half target and no catches. Darnell Washington wasn't much better. Granted, the Steelers didn't have a ton of offensive snaps to get these guys touches. They didn't do much to solve that problem, either.

Rodgers was sacked three times and was frequently under duress. Warren went almost nowhere as a ball carrier with seven carries for 15 yards. That's very little for this group to hang their collective hats on. As we've covered, Rodgers and Warren also were not very good individually in this one, but we can't let these guys off the proverbial hook here either.

Burrow had all day to throw as he dissected this defense. Some of that is on the linebackers, who we'll get to in a minute. Still, with the return of 2025 first-round pick Derrick Harmon from injury, you would have expected these guys to be far more disruptive than they were. They were better in the running game – the Bengals finished with just 78 rushing yards, which is manageable on paper. That total is probably deceptive, though. Chase Brown was able to run well situationally against this defense, and the pass was working so well that he didn't need to do much more.

The Bengals have mastered the art of neutralizing T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig by getting the ball out quickly. That was especially true in this one against DC Patrick Graham's soft zone scheme, which encourages quarterbacks to nibble underneath until they make big mistakes. Burrow doesn't make many. And the Steelers' highly paid trio did little to cause any. All three were basically invisible, and that's unacceptable in a game of this magnitude.

You'd think these guys were gashed deep all night, given Burrow's gaudy 409-yard stat line, but that wasn't really the case. Ja'Marr Chase broke free for a couple of big ones that bolstered his stats, including one in garbage time in the fourth quarter. For the most part, it was otherwise just down-to-down brilliance from the Bengals quarterback. He found seemingly every soft spot in the zone, and the Steelers' defensive backs obliged by missing a lot of tackles and conceding extra yardage. In some ways, these guys did what they were supposed to by keeping the play in front of them. In doing so, however, they proved the limitations of this defensive scheme against the quality quarterbacks the Steelers will face in the playoffs, assuming they make it that far.

McCarthy's offensive play calls did little to get Rodgers into any kind of comfort zone. The execution was also dreadful, which has to land on the head coach coming off 13 days of bye-week rest. As we mentioned above, it's alarming that Graham's defense doesn't seem to have another gear when the zone is getting picked apart by a quarterback capable of executing against it. He needs to find some ways to mix things up if this becomes a first-round playoff matchup later in the year.

What Tennessee HC Josh Heupel said about using 2 QBs in win over Texas A&M appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Tennessee football watched Faizon Brandon fire off one touchdown lob. Yet George MacIntyre took the early snaps against Texas A&M. But was playing both planned by head coach Josh Heupel?

Tennessee boosted its College Football Playoff hopes by beating the Aggies 22-7 Saturday. Heupel became pleased by the play of both.

"Both of them played extremely well. Proud of both of those guys. Big smiles on their faces, excited about the win," Heupel said to reporters afterward.

Brandon, though, stepped in with MacIntyre briefly hurt due to a knee injury. Heupel saw that MacIntyre wanted to head back in. But felt that throwing him back out there was unnecessary.

"George got twisted up on the one pass play… just with where the game was and what we felt like we needed. I didn't feel like it was the right place for George, just dealing with that injury," Heupel said.

MacIntyre orchestrated the opening scoring drive that took 16 plays and ate up 70 yards, culminating in a field goal. Tennessee and MacIntyre still had trouble getting the ball into the end zone, settling for one more field goal. Brandon managed to squeak in the five-yard touchdown pass to lift the Tennessee lead to 16-7 in the third quarter.

So Brandon looked redeemed following an earlier benching in October against Auburn. But the focus shifted to MacIntyre's health. College football insider Pete Nakos, however, shared this big update.

"Tennessee QB George MacIntyre is not expected to miss any time with his knee injury, sources tell On3," Nakos posted on the social media website X, formerly Twitter.

Tennessee now joins Alabama and Texas as the remaining 8-2 teams with two regular season games left.

#2598. Zac Taylor calls Joe Burrow best QB on Earth amid MVP chants

Bengals head coach Zac Taylor assessed quarterback Joe Burrow's remarkable recent performance after a 38-18 rout of the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday night at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football.

Taylor was asked after the game whether he heard MVP chants from the crowd.

"Well, I mean, (it would) be impossible to say anybody's playing better than him," Taylor told reporters after the game. "I'm not watching every game, but I can promise you people that aren't talking about him aren't watching all of our games because if you are, it's really hard to say that this dude's not the best player on planet Earth."

Burrow had 409 passing yards - including 302 in the first half - with four touchdowns before giving way to Joe Flacco in the fourth quarter. Receiver Ja'Marr Chase had the fourth 200+-yard game of his remarkable career.

The first half was particularly ugly for Pittsburgh. NBC Sports analyst and former Bengals receiver Cris Collinsworth said early in the third quarter that he's never seen the Steelers humiliated the way they were in the first half.

"They got smashed tonight," analyst and former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin said. "They ran into a buzzsaw."

#2596. Ex-Guardians catcher Bo Naylor testifies in defense of Emmanuel Clase, Luis Ortiz in MLB pitch-rigging trial

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Former Cleveland Guardians catcher Bo Naylor on Thursday testified in federal court that he perceived nothing untoward about disputed pitches thrown by former All-Star closer Emmanuel Clase and his former Guardians teammate Luis Ortiz, ESPN reports.

Naylor, who played five seasons for the Guardians, appeared as a witness for the defense in the ongoing federal trial in which prosecutors allege that Clase and Ortiz rigged multiple pitches for the benefit of co-conspiring bettors. In Clase's case, he's alleged to have done so in 17 games across a two-year period beginning in May 2023. Naylor, now a member of the Milwaukee Brewers, was catcher for some of Clase's disputed appearances during that span, including seven of the 18 pitches he's alleged to have rigged.

Naylor, a defense witness, was shown video replays of some of the pitches the government alleges were predetermined by Clase or Ortiz as part of the scheme. Naylor was behind the plate for many of them and said they looked like common sliders outside the strike zone. He said the scouting reports on the hitters Ortiz faced during the two pitches in question indicated that sliders low and away would be a "weapon."

In November 2025, Clase and Ortiz were indicted by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York. According to the Department of Justice, both pitchers "agreed in advance with their co-conspirators to throw specific types of pitches and speeds of pitches." The Department of Justice alleged that the pair made at least $450,000 by rigging outings and throwing specific pitches to benefit bettors who wagered on the outcomes of those pitches.

Both Clase and Ortiz pleaded not guilty to those charges in November of last year. Clase and Ortiz have been on administrative leave since late June 2025 while Major League Baseball investigates. MLB has the authority to discipline the pitchers regardless of how the criminal trial plays out.

The pair could face up to 65 years in prison if convicted on the charges of wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy, conspiracy to influence sporting contests by bribery, and money laundering conspiracy.

#2594. Fantasy Football: Joe Burrow stamps MVP case in Week 10 while Christian McCaffrey turns back the clock

I start collecting notes on the games soon after kickoff. And I'm not just jotting down what happened, but an angle on the action. For instance, while the Jacksonville "Trevor Washingtons" were playing well in the first half, the running game was stuck in neutral. However, we (I, mostly) forget how quickly things can change. Sunday wasn't just about early-game narratives flipping, but even perspectives from the previous week getting challenged.

Anyway, let's go through some of the top storylines from Week 10 and what they could mean for fantasy.

Last Wednesday, I made the rest-of-season bold call that Joe Burrow could challenge Josh Allen for the QB1 spot in fantasy. I'll admit my track record on bold calls hasn't been great this season (I've gotten close!). But like my other hot takes, this one was rooted in some reality. Burrow just needed to maintain his pace of play. And if this is the only call I get right, I'm OK with it.

Pittsburgh, with two weeks to prepare, came into the game allowing the third-fewest passing TDs. They were fourth in sack percentage. Their secondary was limiting opposing offenses to the ninth-lowest passing success rate. Since the Bengals were coming back from Madrid, the Steelers had all of the advantages a defense would need outside of playing on their home turf.

And still, No. 9 put up an MVP performance.

Passing Success Rate: 62.2%, 1st (of any QB to play against PIT)

Pittsburgh tried blitzing him throughout the first half and twice to start the third quarter. Burrow was a perfect 11-for-11 for 143 yards. Six of those throws turned into first downs. The Steelers' only sack was on a similar pass-rush concept in the first quarter. Afterward, Burrow was under duress just five more times. This time, it was Ja'Marr Chase who took the spotlight, hoarding 14 of Burrow attempts for an absurd 54.8% share of the air yards. However, it wasn't just about the WRs making big plays. Instead of just pushing the ball downfield, the ancillary options in the short area of the field helped set up the intermediate daggers to keep the offense on schedule.

Chase Brown had his best day of the season on Sunday night. Not only was he back up to a 50% rushing success rate on early downs (first time in a month), but he continued to make plays as a receiver. Even if you take away his two short receiving TDs, half of his catches resulted in a first down. Along with Dohnte Meyers and Drew Sample chipping in, Burrow showed they can sequence dink-and-dunk catches with the Chase or Tee Higgins explosive waiting to catch any defense lacking.

Washington has its own mini-bye after playing on TNF, so it has a few days' head start before the Bengals travel down to Landover in Week 11. But it just gave up almost 300 yards to J.J. McCarthy. And with the way Cincinnati's offense has been putting up points, the MVP chants for Burrow will only intensify.

It was just seven days ago when I was heaping praise on Jordan Love and the Packers' passing attack. The whole operation, minus the occasional drop from Matthew Golden, looked easy. DC Brian Flores reminded Green Bay that defenses can be more complicated from time to time.

The Vikings defense reset Love's single-game, career-high sack total from five to eight. He now has three games in the season with double-digit hits from the opposing defense. Minnesota owns two of them. However, the problem wasn't just Love's health being at risk. And it wasn't that he fell below 250 passing yards for the first time since early October, either. Flores had Love playing a different style of football.

Passing aDOT: 8.6 (Week 10), 10.0 (Last Six Games)

Middle-of-the-Field Throw Rate: 61.5%, 46.6%

Coming into Week 10, Love had the fourth-most yards on throws to the perimeter. He tacked on just 45 against the Vikings. He was fifth in EPA per dropback on throws of 15+ air yards. One, after averaging 9.6 attempts per game of similar depths in Weeks 1-9, Love just threw four similar passes in the divisional rematch. And two, the majority of the completions didn't come until the second half. The one positive was that Love kept the same trust in his WRs as he had in weeks past (complimentary). But, as I mentioned for Golden, his play remained unchanged (derogatory).

To be clear, I'm not knocking Golden for the drop. Love came right back to him on the next drive for the Packers' first explosive play of the game. However, in a game where the margins were already thin, adding to his league-high drop total only helps the people who roster him. Because yet again, Golden (31.0% target rate, 22.0% air yard share) and Christian Watson (17.2%, 22.0%) dominated the opportunities. And not much changed for Tucker Kraft. The Packers used two or more TEs on 61.1% of their offensive plays (season-high), but Kraft's utilization (78.4% route rate, 13.8% target share) didn't dip. Playing the Vikings was just a complete 180-degree shift from their previous opponents. Luckily, they've got the bye week to recalibrate before facing the Rams in Week 12.

I'll answer my own question here. I'd say James Cook III is properly rated. Actually, we answered this question back in August. Players don't just randomly wind up with a single-digit ADP. That's especially the case when their QB turns into a vulture at the goal line. So, it shouldn't be too surprising to see Dalvin's younger brother put on a show.

Honestly, it's better seeing Cook back in this condition compared to last week. And sticking with Buffalo's bout with Minnesota, Cook is the lesser-discussed reason for the Bills coming out on top. Jahmyr Gibbs is the only other RB to face the Vikings this season and churn out more than 100 yards on the ground. And those gains didn't just help the people rostering Cook. In the second half, with a stronger lean on the run (PROE down to -10.3%), his early down runs set up Allen with more manageable passing situations (average 7.2 yards to the sticks). That's where his complementary play to Allen's becomes critical to Buffalo's success. The numbers bear out the same story.

Rushing Success Rate: 47.1%, 10th (out of 18 qualifiers – min. 50% rushing share)

Adj. Yards After Contact per Att.: 3.95, 7th

On a per-touch basis, few have done it better than Cook. Of the 18 RBs with more than half of their team's carries, Cook has seen the highest rate of eight or more defenders in the box (54.5%). And yet, he's one of the five rushers in that same category with a positive EPA per tote. Plus, with Allen leading his offense, even fewer have access to the same number of opportunities. Only Javonte Williams has played more snaps from inside the five-yard line. Of course, Cooks' problem is that less than half of those plays have turned into actual touches (15 of 32).

Cook has been what we wanted Chase Brown to be. Cook can grind out short yards or break off an explosive play like any of his peers. But being a caddy to one of the league's best QBs has its weekly drawbacks. You'll get outings where Allen will have the only rushing scores. But with someone like Cook on your roster, you'll take the highs and lows.

If you played against Christian McCaffrey today, just close your league app.

Hey, sometimes these things happen. In hindsight, with the 49ers going up against Dallas' defense, the chance for a knockout performance was always possible. But seeing it in real time was one of the best performances of 2026.

If there was any credit to give to Dallas' defense, they were at least able to keep McCaffrey bottled up as a rusher. Through two quarters, his eight attempts resulted in just 21 yards on a 12.5% success rate. The same was the case for Kaelon Black. His lone carry picked up four yards. As a rushing unit, the 49ers had just one first down from non-Brock Purdy runners.

I know this section is about McCaffrey, but Black plowing through Caleb Downs for the TD deserved its own highlight. Regardless, rushing success rates for both RBs were up to 40+% to close out the game. But McCaffrey's real damage was done as a receiver.

I realize per-route metrics need more than 17 routes to stabilize. But the video-game results are too gaudy to let slide. Purdy buying time with his legs and pulling multiple defenders forward is the type of offensive harmony you don't see too often. Every target to McCaffrey added 4.2 EPA. Half of his catches turned into explosives.

Unfortunately, the 49ers go from an easier defensive matchup to the Vikings and Seahawks in back-to-back weeks. But with McCaffrey this effective as a receiver, his floor should be worth a start every week.

I can see both sides of the "letting a QB sit behind a veteran" debate. Not everybody's ready to play at the NFL level. Besides, Las Vegas' coaching overhaul was in its infancy, and Kirk Cousins was the ideal operator for HC Klint Kubiak's under-center, play-action offense. But the Raiders planned to start Fernando Mendoza soon anyway. I would've opted for his debut to come against a different opponent, and the results were about as I expected.

Vegas' opening script went as well as Kubiak designed it. The offense marched right down the field, with Mendoza capping off the drive with the same draw play that helped him earn a title. But a few things to consider before adding him to your list of viable streamers. First, the drive started on Seattle's side of the field after Drew Lock fumbled. Second, of the 11-play series, Mendoza threw the ball three times. No pass went farther than four air yards. Most importantly, Brock Bowers was on the field for just two snaps on that drive. And without Mendoza's "WR1," much of the play-calling tendencies that kept the offense on schedule for Cousins went out the window.

The Raiders ran 11-personnel (three-receiver sets) on 65.7% of Mendoza's dropbacks. For reference, their previous high was 58.1% back in Week 2. But here's where playing against Seattle's defense in your first start amplifies the issue. Ten of Mendoza's 19 pressures came in 2.5 seconds or less. And with just one pass-catcher above the 50th percentile in creating separation, Mendoza's average time to throw continued to tick up. Seattle pressured him on 48.7% of his dropbacks, and he did complete over half of his throws under duress. But the result was just two first downs.

We don't know the severity of Bowers' injury yet. And both of the Raiders' opponents before their bye have top-five marks in pressure rate. As a result, it might be toward the end of the season before we see the best of Mendoza and the Raiders.

#2593. MLB rumors: Tarik Skubal's market already hot, contenders eyeing Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is a bit more than a week old and already the hot stove moves and rumors are coming in. We've ranked the top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and built you a calendar of the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Friday's hot stove happenings.

The market for two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, far and away the offseason's best free agent, is already hot, according to the New York Post. Skubal is expected to sign in November, before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, though a deal is not imminent. Talks are underway, however, and his market is moving.

Skubal is expected to sign a record contract at least in total value, and possibly in average annual value. Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers is the largest pitching contract ever given out. Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander's matching $43.3 million salaries with the Mets years ago set the record for the average annual value for a pitcher.

The Dodgers, Mets, Padres, Phillies, and Yankees are among the teams linked to Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports the New York Post. Unless MLB and the MLBPA unexpectedly avoid a lockout, Sato must sign before the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Otherwise, he will return to the Hanshin Tigers for 2027.

We ranked Sato as the fourth-best free agent available this offseason, and the best available position player. He has significant power but also swing-and-miss and defensive concerns at third base, similar to Munetaka Murakami a year ago. Murakami slugged 35 home runs in only 127 games as a rookie this season, providing proof of concept for Sato.

The Nationals have signed center fielder Jacob Young to a four-year extension, reports FanSided. The deal is worth $23 million and includes an $8 million club option for a fifth year. The extension buys out Young's three arbitration years and one free agent year, with a club option for a second free agent year. He's now under Washington's control through 2031.

Young, 27, has always been a superlative defender. He unlocked a new level on offense this season, particularly in the second half, when he hit .301 with a .385 on-base percentage. Young had been speculated as a trade candidate since last offseason, but the new extension locks him in as part of Washington's long-term core.

#2590. Five under-the-radar MLB free agents who could make a big impact next season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is a little more than a week old now and we're still waiting for the first big trade or free agent signing. That isn't unusual, though. The hot stove, like the regular season, is a marathon, not a sprint. A lockout is expected when the collective bargaining agreement ends at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, and there should be a flurry of activity before then.

We ranked the offseason's top 50 free agents, and although it is not a great class, there are dozens of quality players available. You just have to know where to look. Here now are five players who did not rank among our top 50 free agents, but would nonetheless be good options and solid pickups for teams that want to raise their floor and improve their supporting cast.

It was a tale of two seasons for the 29-year-old Bryan Abreu, who had a 5.81 ERA before the All-Star break and a 1.71 ERA after. The under-the-hood estimators, like FIP and xERA, were better in the second half as well, though Abreu lost close to 2 mph off his fastball this year and, not coincidentally, a whole bunch of swings and misses. Abreu is third in appearances and second in innings among relievers since 2022 and it's possible the workload is catching up to him. There's still enough bat-missing ability and late-inning experience here for Abreu to contribute to a contender's bullpen. It just might happen as a seventh-inning guy moving forward, not as the Moment of Truth™ reliever who pitches in the game's biggest moments.

If you're looking for a bottom of the order guy who will take walks and give you 10-15 home runs, that's J.P. Crawford. His defense, specifically his range and arm, has slipped so much in his early 30s that he's no longer a viable shortstop, though he played 33 games at third base this past season. I like him better at second base, but third base works too. Crawford gets on-base at a decent clip and won't strike out excessively, plus he's long been regarded as an excellent teammate and grade-A clubhouse guy. It seems like his time with the Mariners is over and it's for the best. Crawford can go elsewhere, play a new position, and just be part of the lineup rather than one of the faces of the franchise.

Due to injury and ineffectiveness, it looked like Sean Newcomb was on his way out of baseball two years ago. He then reinvented himself as a sinker/curveball guy and carved out a nice second phase to his career as a workhorse utility reliever who won't beat himself with walks (an early career bugaboo) and will limit hard contact in the air. Newcomb, 33, worked at least 90 innings the last two seasons while pitching in every possible role. He closed out games, worked high leverage as a setup guy, soaked up innings in long relief, and opened a few times as well. Newcomb is likely miscast as a go-to bullpen option, though he can be a valuable third or fourth option for a contender. The utility reliever is all the rage these days and Newcomb fits the profile to a T.

Now 35, Emilio Pagán was sensational after returning from a hamstring injury in July, pitching to a 1.88 ERA with 34 strikeouts and only five walks in his final 28 ⅔ innings. The downside is the same as it's always been: Pagán is exceptionally home run prone (career 1.51 HR/9), which is a bad trait for a late-inning reliever who pitches almost exclusively in close games. His fastball remains firm, though, and his splitter is an elite swing-and-miss pitch that allows him to neutralize righties and lefties. As long as you're willing to live with the home run risk, Pagán remains a capable high-leverage reliever, one who is not out of place pitching important innings for a contending team.

Platoon DHs are not the hottest commodity, but Joc Pederson fills the role about as well as anyone in the game. He's a left-handed hitter, so he's on the heavy side of the platoon, and he authored a .245/.338/.496 line with terrific ball-tracking data (exit velocity, etc.) against righties. If you must play him in the field, Pederson can stand in right field or at first base for about six innings before being subbed out for a defensive replacement. He's essentially a bat-only player, though. Pederson will turn 35 in April and he's still a powerful and productive hitter against righties and an elite clubhouse vibes dude.

#2588. LebRon James steps into 3rd on NBA's career assist list as 76ers beat Pacers

PHILADELPHIA (AP) — LeBron James had 11 assists and moved into third on the NBA's career list, and he added 15 points and six rebounds to lead the Philadelphia 76ers past the Indiana Pacers 131-124 on Sunday.

James, who turns 42 next month, dished one to VJ Edgecombe in the fourth quarter for assist 12,092 to pass Jason Kidd on the career list. John Stockton and Chris Paul are 1-2 in NBA history.

Jaylen Brown scored 31 points and Tyrese Maxey added 27 for the Sixers.

Pascal Siakam led the Pacers with 31 points and former Sixer Kelly Oubre Jr. added 16.

James continued an early habit in his first season with the Sixers in picking his spot to take control of a game.

PHOENIX (AP) — Luka Doncic scored 43 points and Los Angeles stretched their winning streak to eight games by holding off Phoenix.

Los Angeles played without second-leading scorer Austin Reaves due to a bruised heel suffered against Milwaukee on Wednesday.

It did little to slow down the NBA's top scoring team — through three quarters.

The Lakers led by 31 late in the third quarter, but the Suns charged back in the fourth behind Collin Gillespie. He scored 12 of his 26 points in the final quarter and pulled the Suns within 126-121 on a driving layup with 1:05 left.

Quentin Grimes banked in a 3-pointer with 34 seconds left and Doncic sealed it with two free throws.

Doncic, the NBA's leading scorer, hit five 3-pointers and went 12 for 14 on free throws for his sixth 40-point game this season. Grimes went 5 of 6 from 3 to finish with 22 points.

TORONTO (AP) — Jalen Brunson made a tiebreaking 3-pointer with 33 seconds remaining in overtime and New York beat Toronto, their 14th straight win over the Raptors.

Brunson scored 28 points, and Karl-Anthony Towns had 28 points and 17 rebounds for the Knicks, who trailed by 13 points in the fourth quarter.

Landry Shamet scored 23 points and OG Anunoby had 21 against his former team as the defending NBA champions snapped a two-game losing streak.

Scottie Barnes scored 30 points and Jamal Shead added 19 but the Raptors lost their fourth straight and seventh in nine.

Toronto has led by double digits in each of its past three defeats. The Raptors couldn't hold a 22-point lead against Boston on Wednesday, and blew a 17-point edge at Philadelphia on Thursday.

Immanuel Quickley scored 17 points, RJ Barrett had 14 and Jakob Poeltl 11. Collin Murray-Boyles had a season-high 13 rebounds for the Raptors.

SACRAMENTO, Calif. (AP) — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored 37 points in three quarters to help Oklahoma City beat Sacramento and end a three-game losing streak.

Gilgeous-Alexander shot 13 for 20 from the field, 4 for 5 from 3-point range and made all seven free throws. He played only 29 minutes, perhaps the only thing keeping him from a second consecutive game with 40 or more points.

He has scored 31 or more in his last three games.

Rookie Aday Mara had 16 points and 12 rebounds off the bench for the Thunder, who led by 27 points. Ajay Mitchell had 14 points, and Isaiah Hartenstein pulled down 11 rebounds.

Rookie Darius Acuff Jr. had 26 points and six rebounds for the Kings, who fell to 1-12 and are 0-8 at home. They fell to 0-6 on a seven-game homestand. Zach LaVine did not suit up for the Kings due to an illness.

BOSTON (AP) — Jayson Tatum scored 32 points in 30 minutes on a night Boston set a franchise record for its lead at the end of the opening period on the way to a win over Dallas.

Derrick White added 16 points and Jordan Walsh 11 to help Boston win its sixth straight and for the 11th time in 12 games.

Tatum had 21 of his points in the third quarter, connecting on 6 of 9 shots and knocking down four 3s. He scored 13 straight points to end the period.

Boston pulled its starters after that but still pulled ahead by 41 in the final quarter.

WASHINGTON (AP) — Amen Thompson scored 26 points and Kevin Durant added 25 to help Houston rout Washington for their fourth straight win.

The Rockets also held Trae Young scoreless for the first time in his NBA career. He missed all five of his shots and had previous scored in all 511 of his prior career games with the Hawks and Wizards.

Alperen Sengun added 19 points and eight assists and eight rebounds for the Rockets, who had a season-high for points.

Alex Sarr had 24 points and AJ Dybantsa added 16 for the Wizards. Dybantsa was 6-for-18 from the field. The Wizards have now lost seven games in a row after a 4-3 start to the season. Their last win came on Nov. 2 against the Magic.

Washington went back-and-forth with Houston for the first quarter, but dominant second and third quarters by the Rockets paved the way for the blowout win. They outscored the Wizards 37-23 in the second and 46-34 in the third to pull away. Houston also outrebounded Washington 55-36.

INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — Darius Garland scored 27 points, Max Strus had 14 off the bench and Los Angeles beat Charlotte for the 17th straight time.

Derrick Jones Jr. and Isaiah Jackson each scored 13 points, while Keaton Wagler and Gradey Dick had 12 apiece as the Clippers overcame a 13-point deficit in the third quarter to win for the third time in four games following a 1-7 start.

Coby White scored 21 points and Naz Reid added 17 for the Hornets, who lost for the eighth time in their past nine games and fell to 0-2 at the start of a four-game road trip. Coach Charles Lee was ejected when he received a pair of technical fouls in a 17-second stretch of the third quarter.

The Hornets haven't defeated the Clippers since Nov. 18, 2017. Their last road win in the series was Feb. 28, 2009.

SALT LAKE CITY (AP) — Dylan Harper had 31 points and nine rebounds to rally San Antonio to a victory over Utah, giving them their 12th straight win, while sending the Jazz to a 12th straight loss.

Victor Wembanyama finished with 26 points, 11 rebounds, six assists, and five blocks for the Spurs. Stephon Castle added 20 points and nine assists. Keldon Johnson had 11 points and 10 boards. San Antonio outscored the Jazz 27-5 in fastbreak points.

Mo Bamba scored 26 points, while going 6 of 6 from 3-point range, to lead Utah. Darryn Peterson scored 17 points for the Jazz. Keyonte George finished with 13 points and eight assists and Brice Sensabaugh added 14 points and seven rebounds off the bench.

San Antonio trailed for much of the fourth quarter until Harper tied it at 100 on back-to-back 3s and then Castle hit a pair of free throws to put the Spurs up 102-100 with 2:30 left.

Castle's steal and dunk with 47.2 seconds remaining capped a 14-4 run and extended San Antonio's lead to 108-102.

MILWAUKEE (AP) — Nickeil Alexander-Walker and CJ McCollum each scored 20 points and Onyeka Okongwu had 16 and 11 rebounds as Atlanta erased a 22-point second-quarter deficit to defeat Milwaukee.

Jalen Johnson added 14 points and 11 rebounds and Corey Kispert had 14 off the bench for the Hawks (8-6), who had lost back-to-back games coming in.

Kasparas Jakucionis scored a career high 25 points, Gary Trent Jr. had 18, Kyle Kuzma 14 and Brayden Burries 13 for Milwaukee.

The Bucks (1-13) lost a 10th straight game and are off to their worst start in 52 years, when they lost 13 of their first 14 in 1974-75 without an injured Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, per Sportradar.

The Bucks sprinted to a 37-18 lead after the first quarter, led by Kuzma's 12 points. Milwaukee shot 58% in the period.

Milwaukee built a 22-point lead early in the second quarter before Atlanta stormed back to take a 55-53 lead at the half on Dyson Daniels' layup just ahead of the horn.

The 2026-27 MLB offseason is a bit more than a week old and already the hot stove moves and rumors are coming in. We've ranked the top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and built you a calendar of the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Saturday's hot stove happenings.

Future Hall of Famer Max Scherzer will pitch in "lockout games" this offseason to determine whether he will continue his career, reports the New York Post. The collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Players on opposing teams work out together throughout the offseason and figure to put together games to stay sharp during the lockout.

Scherzer, 42, made 18 starts around injuries with the Blue Jays this season. If 2026 was his final season, he went out with a bang. Scherzer struck out seven in seven innings of one-run ball in Game 162. He is currently ninth all-time with 3,557 strikeouts, three behind former Tigers teammate Justin Verlander. We did not rank Scherzer among our top 50 free agents.

Multiple teams have interest in free agent Ty France, according to The Athletic. A deal could come together quickly. France had a career year in 2026 after opening his stance a bit, which unlocked more hard-hit ability. He's a terrific defensive first baseman as well. We ranked France as the offseason's 23rd-best free agent, and the second-best available first baseman.

It's unclear which teams are in the hunt for France, though there is no shortage of contenders who could use the 32-year-old. The Diamondbacks, Guardians, Mets, Rangers, and of course Padres stand out as potential landing spots. Given his career year and the surprising lack of right-handed power in the game right now, France could command a multi-year contract

The Fubon Guardians of the Chinese Professional Baseball League have posted righty reliever Jyun-Yue Tseng for MLB teams, reports the Associated Press. Officially, Tseng has until Dec. 22 to sign, though the expected lockout means his signing deadline is really Dec. 1. We did not rank him among our top 50 free agents.

Tseng, 25, pitched for Chinese Taipei in the World Baseball Classic in 2023 and 2026. He saved 25 games with a 1.80 ERA and 65 strikeouts in 52 ⅓ innings this past season. Tseng's fastball typically sits in the mid-90s but has run as high as 100 mph in the past. His secondary pitches need work to carve out an MLB career as more than a middle reliever.

#2585. Brewers bash champion Dodgers to brink of NLCS sweep; CBS Sports Preseason All-America team revealed

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here.

One of the biggest benefits of the NIL era is that college basketball has more elite talent than ever, now that players are returning for bigger paychecks instead of bolting for NBA money at the first opportunity.

That made selecting our 2026-27 CBS Sports Preseason All-America teams especially difficult, but our experts nailed it. Each of the three teams features players who will be performing at the next level very soon, but the best of those might be Florida superstar Thomas Haugh.

As our own Isaac Trotter explains, if Haugh can improve his range shooting, he won't have to wait long to hear his name called in the 2027 NBA Draft.

When it comes to how the talent broke down by conference, it was a a pretty level playing field for the most part.

Not to spoil anyting, but Arizona freshman Caleb Holt did not make the cut. He did, however, turn some heads in the Wildcats' exhibition game.

Loyalty is an excellent quality to have in a friend or partner. It's also why we love dogs.

It should not be quite as prevalent among college football coaches, some of whom have been undone because they did what was comfortable, not what was necessarily best for the team.

Our own John Talty highlighted five high-profile coaches who have been loyal to a fault, making hires and personnel decisions that have come back to haunt them. One of those coaches is Mike Elko. After a shaky season from Marcel Reed in 2025, Texas A&M chose not to pursue an upgrade in the portal.

Instead, the Aggies gave Reed a major payday, and they'll miss the College Football Playoff because of it.

Look, it can happen to the best of us. Dan Lanning and Dabo Swinney wound up on the list, despite the success that those two have had throughout their careers.

Steve Sarkisian is another coach who has fallen into the trap of being too loyal, but he may have a huge decision on his hands in the offseason. Arch Manning has struggled enough that another year in college should be on the table. If that happens, would Sark welcome back Manning with open arms, despite his shortcomings?

Finally, one person for whom loyalty is no an issue is Missouri QB Austin Simmons. After Trinidad Chambliss won the starting job at Ole Miss last year, Simmons didn't feel the need to stick around, but there won't be bitterness when Simmons returns to Oxford this weekend.

#2584. NBA's biggest winners and losers of the week: Luka's Lakers look amazing, are Hornets regretting LaMelo trade?

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

At the risk of tempting fate, we're coming off of a pretty optimistic week in the NBA. The late-October rush of season-altering injuries has seemingly slowed down. The quality of basketball has been excellent, and stars are making history. Things in the NBA are so positive right now that there are multiple, ongoing seven-game winning streaks that won't be featured in our winners of the week.

So... who beat out the trimmed-for-space Golden State Warriors and San Antonio Spurs? And who are our losers in a week full of winners? Let's dive into our rankings from the week that was.

No Jalen Williams. No Cason Wallace. No Chet Holmgren. And also, no losses. That's the week that the Thunder just had, first sweeping their season series with the Cleveland Cavaliers before blowing the doors off of the Memphis Grizzlies and Washington Wizards by 70 combined points. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander averaged just under 36 points in the 4-0 stretch, but the story here is Oklahoma City finding a new formula to compensate for all of these absences.

The Thunder built their historic defense around turnover generation, leading the NBA on that front in their 2025 championship season and finishing No. 2 a year ago. They've fallen to 21st as of Sunday, accepting that they simply cannot play as aggressively without their core defenders as they once did. Instead, they're selling out to protect the basket. They allowed the second-fewest points in the paint per game a season ago ... and have trimmed five of them off of their average this season. They've even started Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara together in two of their past three games, though they've shared minimal possessions.

The defense may not be generating turnovers, but the offense isn't committing any either. Oklahoma City has taken its turnover-prevention offense to the extreme. The Thunder are averaging 231.6 passes per game, 10 fewer than any team in the tracking era. Only the Spurs and the Philadelphia 76ers, both healthy championship contenders, are turning the ball over less. This "no passes means no turnovers" offense only works if the individual creators are up to snuff. Gilgeous-Alexander obviously fits the bill, but now, so does Ajay Mitchell. The Thunder are scoring over 1.2 points per possession when Mitchell shoots out of pick-and-roll, good for the 94th percentile league-wide. He's scoring just under 25 points per 36 minutes, more than Cade Cunningham and just below Deni Avdija and Austin Reaves.

Oh yeah, and they made a trade with the Sacramento Kings. I'm comfortable calling any team lucky enough to trade with the Kings an automatic winner for that week, especially when they're acquiring a guard on a rookie contract. Do the words "Tyrese Haliburton" mean nothing to you, Sacramento? Nique Clifford certainly won't live up to that prematurely dealt King, but there's a parallel here to Davion Mitchell, another former first-round pick the Kings dealt who has since blossomed with the Miami Heat. You should trust no team's ability to evaluate players less than Sacramento's ... and no team's more than Oklahoma City's. If Sam Presti thinks Clifford can help the injury-ravaged Thunder, I'm inclined to believe that a price of two second-round picks is a bargain. All in all, it was about as perfect a week as the Thunder could have asked for.

He's averaging 40 points! This isn't a handful of games against terrible teams anymore. The Portland Trail Blazers have been great defensively against everyone except the Los Angeles Lakers because Luka has blitzed them for 94 points in two meetings. Of the 20 highest individual point totals so far this season, Dončić comes in at No. 1, No. 2, No. 5, No. 12, No. 17 and No. 18. The two biggest pillars of the MVP race are scoring and winning. Clearly, he's got the scoring down.

So far, winning hasn't been an issue either. The Lakers are 9-2, and it's almost exclusively because of the offense he runs. As of Sunday, the Lakers ranked 23rd in rebounding rate, 23rd in defense and 25th in turnover rate. It hasn't mattered because the offense is No. 1 with a bullet. The Lakers are roughly 34 points per 100 possessions better when he plays than when he sits, yet they were still able to pull off a critical road win over the Detroit Pistons on Sunday without him. The Lakers are a regular-season wins machine, and Dončić is the engineer.

It's not just the raw total, either. It's how this is all happening. Dončić currently leads the NBA in both 3-point attempts and free-throw attempts. When James Harden was doing that a decade ago, it was considered such witchcraft that defenders started standing behind him and guarding him with their hands behind their backs. I look forward to seeing what sort of nonsense teams concoct against Dončić if this continues. He's making 30-footers look like layups. He's giving Laker fans the sort of individual offense they haven't seen since Kobe Bryant's peak. Enjoy it. Stretches like this don't come around often.

The underlying message of the Ball trade was that the Charlotte Hornets did not think he could be relied upon as a franchise player. Given the questions surrounding his durability, his defense and even his maturity, it wasn't a crazy thought. The idea that he would fare better in a secondary role in Minnesota made plenty of sense. He and Anthony Edwards looked like one of the NBA's best duos in the season's opening week. Then Edwards got hurt, and Ball was suddenly back to being the centerpiece. How has he responded? Well, let's look at the team numbers since Edwards went down:

It's a tiny sample, but thus far, Ball is impacting his new Timberwolves teammates in much the same way he affected his former Hornets (don't worry, we'll get to them!). Everyone else's life gets vastly simpler on offense when they're fortunate enough to play with LaMelo Ball. Even without Edwards, he's more than kept the Timberwolves afloat. When Edwards eventually returns, this team is a genuine contender in the Western Conference.

With Ball, the Hornets had the best offense in the NBA from early December through the end of last season. Well, without him, they're last. By a mile. They're last in basically everything. No team has a lower true shooting percentage. No team turns the ball over. Ready for a jarring stat? We covered Oklahoma City's "no pass" offense earlier. Well, the Thunder are averaging more assists than the Hornets this season ... on 65 fewer passes per game.

The Hornets knew they were getting worse when they made the trade. It was a conscious choice: take a step back, take a few spins in the revamped lottery, accumulate assets that could be flipped later. The Hornets felt like they were destined to be a perpetual middle-of-the-standings team with Ball. They traded him in the hopes that getting worse now could make them championship contenders later.

Their fans probably could have lived with a small step back. What we've seen thus far has been a disaster. Not all of it is their fault. They've barely had Coby White or Kon Knueppel -- and Knueppel will be about another four weeks at least with a hamstring strain. Brandon Miller, the other cornerstone here who just signed a $209 million contract, is shooting 26% from 3 and below 36% from the floor because of how overburdened he currently is. A step back may have been the idea, but nobody thought it would be this bad, nor did many assume Ball would be this good for Minnesota. It doesn't change Charlotte's long-term outlook, but it makes the present that much more painful. All of the goodwill from last year's turnaround has seemingly evaporated.

We came into the season relatively certain about how the Western Conference was tiered. The Spurs and Thunder were at the top. The Lakers, the Wolves, the Houston Rockets and the Denver Nuggets would land between No. 3 and No. 6 in some order. After that? Well, no one gave much thought to the Play-In Tournament. The East was supposed to be the deep conference. That's an opinion we cycle through every four or five years. Every year is supposed to be the East's year, and then it isn't. When the Memphis Grizzlies and Portland Trail Blazers were lighting on the world on fire, it seemed as though the West's depth had triumphed yet again.

It still is, on balance. The Warriors and the Dallas Mavericks, for instance, are strongly exceeding expectations. But the early excitement over Memphis and Portland, at least, is starting to wane. The Grizzlies traded a six-game winning streak for a three-game losing streak. The Blazers walked into the hardest stretch of their schedule thus far, took a loss to the Lakers and then got smacked around by the Spurs. With two games against the Thunder coming, Portland is seemingly coming back down to Earth. For a moment there, the New Orleans Pelicans looked as though they were figuring some things out on a four-game winning streak, but back-to-back losses have them out of the Play-In picture, at least for now.

These teams are still better than we figured they'd be, and there's still a bit of wiggle room in the West. Denver, for instance, looks enormously vulnerable. But the Spurs have won eight in a row. The Thunder have righted the ship. The Lakers, Wolves and Rockets are all as good as we thought or better. For a moment there, it looked like we were due some surprises out West. For now, it seems as though order has mostly been restored.

It is still much, much too early to draw any meaningful conclusions about lottery reform, but an early topic thus far this season has been how bad the bottom of the league still is despite the removal of the tanking incentive. With almost three weeks in the books, there are seven teams with either one or two victories. Between those seven teams, there are only three total victories over teams above .500. The Kings beat the Mavericks ... without Kyrie Irving. The Orlando Magic beat the Toronto Raptors ... without Kawhi Leonard, and their victory over the New York Knicks at least came with Jalen Suggs in the lineup. If Suggs and Paolo Banchero were healthy, the Magic would likely not be in this class.

Essentially, when the worst teams are playing against the best ones at anything resembling full strength, they've been hopeless. Inevitably, a certain number of teams is just going to be bad whether or not they're trying to lose. In fact, given this year's specific outlook, it's not even clear how motivated any of these bottom-tier teams are to actually win. The relegation zone isn't a threat to the Milwaukee Bucks, Brooklyn Nets, Utah Jazz or Los Angeles Clippers because they don't actually control their own first-round picks. You could argue that being in the relegation zone would actually be advantageous to the Chicago Bulls in order to minimize their odds of getting a top-five pick in the bad 2027 draft, because doing so, in concert with their No. 4 pick in 2026, would lock them out of a top-five pick in the stronger 2028 class.

We might not see the sort of overt tanking we've gotten in years past, but the question here is whether or not that will actually matter. With so many of these teams having minimal incentives to win, will they still shut down key players midway through the season? Even if they don't, will attendance and television ratings be better for these teams down the stretch just because they're nominally trying? We're months away from even starting to get answers to these questions, but any notions that reform would create 30 competitive teams have been quickly dismissed. Even in October and November, some teams are already pretty tough to watch.
